https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.author: Shrai Popat (now) and Tom Ambrose (earlier)
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.text:
Some Democrats who missed key procedural vote to impeach Pete Hegseth blame traffic jam in DC – US politics live
11 Democrats missed vote, which failed 211-204 and effectively killed effort to oust Hegseth for now; Trump hails ‘exoneration of a Great American Patriot’
Some Democrats who missed key procedural vote to impeach Pete Hegseth blame traffic jam in Washington
Some Democrats, out of the 11 who missed the key procedural vote on Tuesday to impeach Pete Hegseth, blamed a traffic jam in Washington DC for their inability to make it to the US Capitol in time.
By a vote of 211-204, Republicans referred the articles of impeachment to the judiciary committee – effectively killing the effort to oust Hegseth.
Since several outgoing Republicans were not back in Washington, if those Democrats voted to block the move the impeachment resolution it would have headed to the House floor for a full debate and vote.
On social media, a number of representatives said that they were stuck behind a motorcade that meant they missed the voting window.
A spokesperson for Congresswoman Melanie Stansbury, of New Mexico, said she was “blocked from entering the Capitol to vote due a traffic incident and a police escort of a bus during the vote. When she reached the chamber the vote had just gaveled out”.
Meanwhile, Representative Laura Gillen, of New York, similarly blamed the “same police escort blocking the Capitol when Republicans closed the vote”.
Illinois congressman Johnathan Jackson cited the same reason in a post on X.
Axios reported that some of the House Democrats who votes were on their way back from a political action committee event that is focused on electing pro-choice Democratic women to office.
Minority leader Hakeem Jeffries is now facing criticism for apparently failing to pressure members of his party to be present for a crucial vote.
When asked by reporters about the absences on Tuesday, Jeffries said that he had not “had a conversation with anyone on the floor team about what may or may not have happened in terms of the Hegseth resolution”.
He added that the resolution would likely be revived: “This is not the end of it. It’s just the beginning.”
Democrat Colom still leads in nail-biting US Senate race in Mississippi
Democrat Scott Colom is still leading the extemely close US Senate race in Mississippi against Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith.
Colom is up by more than 3,000 votes, with 98% counted. A reminder that Tuesday 10 November was the ballot deadline in the state, which means that we can expect consequential drops today.
If Colom wins, it will be a remarkable upset in a state that hasn’t elected a Democrat as senator since 1982, and in a state that Donald Trump carried by 22 points in 2024.

Democrat Eileen Laubacher is leading Republican incumbent Lauren Boebert in the race for Colorado’s fourth congressional district. As of now, Laubacher is up by over 3,300 votes with 98% counted.
Boebert, a Maga firebrand and loyal ally to Donald Trump, is trying to hold on to the reliably red district that Trump carried by 18 points in 2024. If Laubacher wins, she would also be the first Democrat to win the seat since 2009.
Donald Trump celebrates federal judge's decision to allow his $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed
After a federal judge has allowed Donald Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against the BBC to proceed, the president heralded the move on Truth Social.
“A Huge Victory against Fake News BBC, a terrible abuser of the truth, just handed down by highly respected District Court Judge, Jeffrey T. Kuntz,” Trump wrote. “We will continue fighting against, and defeating, all of those who try to deceive the American People!”
The president is suing the broadcaster over an edited clip that made it appear that Trump told his supporters to storm the US Capitol on 6 January 2021.
In honor of veterans day, the president will head to Arlington National Cemetery with first lady Melania Trump for a wreath laying ceremony and to deliver remarks at 11am ET. After, Trump will be back in the White House for meetings.
If there was one obvious conclusion from Democrats’ sweeping victories in the mid-term elections on Tuesday, it seemed to be that the Republican effort to redraw congressional districts in their favor backfired.
Starting last summer, Trump and Republican allies undertook an aggressive effort to redraw congressional districts, reconfiguring the lines to give Republican candidates an advantage. Ahead of the midterms, Republicans redrew 15 seats to their advantage. After Tuesday’s election, they appear poised to lose all but two of them. “It was definitely the wrong move,” an unnamed House Republican told Fox News. “One of the truisms in politics is never to overreach. We did and that was part of the reason for the backlash.”
The Republicans losses included defeats in Texas, Florida and North Carolina where Republicans hoped to pick up as many as 10 combined congressional seats.
“The maps themselves did fail, and failed quite epically,” said John Bisognano, the president of the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, a Democratic redistricting group. “I would also argue the idea itself was an even bigger failure. Allowing an environment to be created around you in which everyone begins to realize how deeply corrupt this administration is and how fearful they are of the American people in elections, so much so that their main tactical path forward is going to be to redraw maps to steal as many voters as they can.”
But even though Republicans failed to pick up nearly all of the new seats they drew, it would be misleading to say that gerrymandering did not work at all in this election, said Nicholas Stephanopoulos, a professor at Harvard who studies redistricting. Republicans didn’t pick up the seats because Democrats had the strongest midterm elections in half a century.
Treasury chief Scott Bessent is reportedly latest Trump official to move to military base
The US Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, has relocated from his home in the Washington area to a military base after an Iranian threat against his life, the New York Times has reported.
Bessent has spearheaded a US push to cripple Iran’s economy since the start of the Middle East war, vowing “economic asphyxiation” of the Islamic republic through a web of sanctions.
He is one of a number of senior figures in the Trump administration including the secretary of state, Marco Rubio, and the new chief of staff, Stephen Miller, to leave their home to live on a military base or protected housing.
The US national intelligence chief, Jay Clayton, said last month that Tehran had “substantially increased” its efforts to target Americans in the Middle East and beyond.
These include intensifying the targeting of current and former US officials such as Bessent, the NYT reported on Tuesday, citing three sources familiar with the matter.
Iranian plotting against US officials has reached a “more advanced stage”, according to the anonymous sources, but the severity of the threats against Bessent was unclear.
Washington ordered non-essential US embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia last month, after increasing attacks from Tehran-backed Houthi fighters.
Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Moscow on Thursday, then meet Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin after their trip to Russia, Kushner said.
Kushner, US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law, said talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi were a “first good step“.
Sanders says he will not support Schumer for Senate Democratic leader
Senator Bernie Sanders has confirmed that he will not be supporting senator Chuck Schumer as the Democratic majority leader in the new Congress, setting up a confrontation after the party’s sweep to power in the midterm elections.
Sanders was joined by Democratic senator Elissa Slotkin of Michigan at a news conference at the Capitol, and together they said there needs to be a new generation of leadership and a vigorous debate about the party’s direction and future, AP reported.
A number of incoming Democratic senators have echoed the call, signaling that they would support another candidate over Schumer.
“The time is now for change,” said Sanders, the independent from Vermont and essentially the father of modern progressivism in the US. “And I will not be supporting Chuck to be reelected as the Democratic leader.”
Slotkin, who said she is not actively seeking the job herself, explained that she wants to see potential Senate leaders present a full plan about the priorities for the new majority. “I’m a no until and unless I see that from anyone,” she said.
The showdown has been building as Democrats swept across the Senate map to flip Republican-held seats far beyond those that were initially competitive, including in Texas, Kansas and South Carolina.
Schumer recruited high-profile candidates that helped secure the majority, including senator-elect Sherrod Brown in Ohio and senator-elect Roy Cooper in North Carolina.
But his preferred candidates also lost primaries in Michigan and Maine, with the progressive candidates prevailing and then going on to win their general elections.
Nancy Pelosi was one of 11 Democratic politicians to miss the Pete Hegseth impeachment vote.
If just eight of them had turned up to vote with their colleagues, the motion would have passed and the articles for impeachment would have moved forward.
The other Democrats recorded as not voting were Julia Brownley, Lou Correa, Laura Gillen of New York, Steven Horsford of Nevada, Jonathan Jackson of Illinois, Brittany Pettersen of Colorado, Melanie Stansbury of New Mexico, Stevens of Michigan, Marilyn Strickland of Washington and Frederica Wilson of Florida, the Daily Beast reported.
House Republicans blocked an effort to impeach Hegseth, rejecting allegations that the defense secretary had repeatedly violated the constitution through his handling of the Iran war and other conflicts globally.
A motion to refer Thomas Massie’s eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth to committee passed in the House, 211-204.
The Pentagon declared “total victory” after the vote and Donald Trump celebrated the vote as an “EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot”.
GOP branded 'sinking ship' as House Republicans block efforts to impeach Hegseth
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
Republican representative Thomas Massie compared the GOP with passengers content to go down with the Titanic after colleagues thwarted his effort to impeach defense secretary Pete Hegseth.
The vote came a week after Republicans lost control of the Senate and House of Representatives in their worst midterm election in more than a half century, and underscored how lawmakers remain wary of crossing Donald Trump, who has signaled his continued support for Hegseth.
“They know it’s a sinking ship but committed to stay on board,” Massie, a Republican congressman who lost his primary after breaking with the president, said.
Top Democrats announced their support for the resolution, but Republicans moved to kill it by referring it to the judiciary committee. Their motion succeeded on Tuesday, by a 211-204 vote, largely along party lines. Massie was the sole Republican to oppose the motion, along with all Democrats.
Trump, who was twice impeached, celebrated what he hailed as the “EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot” and lashed out at Massie for forcing the vote.
“The Democrats continue to weaponize and abuse the United States of America,” Trump said on Truth Social. “They must be stopped!”
The Pentagon, meanwhile, declared “total victory”. “The referral of these baseless impeachment articles to the House judiciary committee marks total victory for Secretary Hegseth, the Department of War, and the American warfighter,” Sean Parnell, a department spokesperson, wrote in a social media post.
Some 11 Democratic representatives skipped the vote, the Daily Beast reported earlier this morning, causing the articles of impeachment to fail. Among those to miss the vote was Nancy Pelosi.
If eight of them had voted with fellow Democrats the measure could have proceeded.
House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries said he would talk to members about whether to mount a new impeachment effort in the next Congress in January when the Democrats who triumphed in the midterm take their seats. “We’ll have that conversation at the appropriate time,” he said.

https://www.theguardian.com/games/2026/n.title: How years of research built Grand Theft Auto VI’s obsessively detailed world
https://www.theguardian.com/games/2026/n.author: Keza MacDonald
https://www.theguardian.com/games/2026/n.text:
In 2015, a group of Grand Theft Auto developers from Rockstar North took their first trips to Miami to do field research for the next game in the phenomenally popular crime series. “Before you’re doing hyper-organised research trips, you’re immersing yourself in the place and its history, the vibe of it,” Rob Nelson, one of the lead developers on GTA VI, tells me. “[You see] the physical places you want to move characters through, the experiences you want them to have, and the juxtaposition between the extremes of society that are in Miami.”
I wondered: did people ever recognise them on any of their research trips? Did locals know what they were doing? This is the biggest game in the world, after all; I imagine it would be difficult to go entirely undercover. “We’re always semi-undercover,” he says. “But if you have a bunch of dorks going through a terrifying neighbourhood, you do stick out a bit.”
Grand Theft Auto VI is finally out next week, more than 10 years since those first exploratory trips. A few weeks ago, I spent the day at Rockstar North’s headquarters in Edinburgh, watching as Nelson and fellow senior exec Jennifer Kolbe took me through Vice City, the fictional version of Miami that has emerged from all that work. The setting always comes first for Rockstar games: the developers immerse themselves in the real-life version of the place they want to create, before they ask what they want to do within it and what they want to offer players. From there emerge the story that Rockstar’s writers want to tell and the characters players will later meet. This time that story is about a criminal couple on the run named Jason and Lucia.
Grand Theft Auto V (2013) and Red Dead Redemption 2 (2018) conjure fascinatingly detailed versions of the US: one a microcosm of California, the other of the old west. GTA VI takes us to Leonida, virtual Florida, and as with Rockstar’s previous games it is gratuitously, absurdly detailed, from the macro level to the micro; from architecture and geography down to the smallest of details – such as the clothes that the pedestrians are wearing, the street art, the flyers on cafe walls and the insides of fridges. As Nelson and I freely explored Vice City, we discussed the effort and motivations that went into the making of this ultra-maximalist game. You can read more about it in the Guardian’s Saturday magazine later this week.
Grand Theft Auto VI was made by an enormous team of almost 5,000 people, but there is a relatively small number of decision-makers at the top, most of whom have been at Rockstar for a very long time. (Lead writer Rupert Humphries, for instance, has been at the company since 2008.) They each take responsibility for the elements of the game that they are most suited to and that they care about most. “The game is so vast that no one person could hold enough of it in their heads,” Nelson tells me. His purview is design, narrative and animation, with a little casting on the side: Nelson’s background is in character art and animation, and his attention to detail is abundantly evident in his demonstration of the game. He takes huge delight in showing me tiny details, such as the way that Jason eats a hot dog or how, as he walks around a gas station, he can take bites of a donut with one hand while sipping a beer with the other.
When Jason starts running, he hikes the six-pack of beers he’s carrying into the crook of his arm, the liquid inside the bottles sloshing around. At one point in my Vice City ridealong, Nelson gets briefly upset during a jewellery store stick-up when the placement of one of the security guards’ feet doesn’t look right. The level of detail in this game is simply out of reach for any other game developer thanks to Rockstar’s abundance of money and time, and the patience from its parent company, Take-Two Interactive.
Rockstar’s worlds are believable because, despite their rampant excess, they are grounded in the real places they are based on and real experiences developers had in those places. Jennifer Kolbe says that during research for Grand Theft Auto IV, which was set in the New-York-inspired Liberty City, “people who had lived in New York all their lives were going to places they would never go to ... We then give that experience to players.”
Nelson reminisces about staying out in a Miami nightclub until 4am and then getting up a few hours later to be driven around a racetrack with a momentous hangover. They went on a ridealong with cops in South Beach, and hung out in weird bars in the Florida Keys. “Some of our team, especially the artists, are very intrepid,” he says. “They’ll go wandering in all sorts of places with their cameras. They’re fearless.”
Rockstar is famous for its depictions of the US – particularly American cities. But I have always wondered what this team could do in a different setting. Could Rockstar ever envision a GTA set outside of America? “Never say never, but there’s still so much to do in America,” Nelson says. I ask whether Rockstar’s outsider status, as a bunch of developers based mostly outside of the US (though it has offices in New York and San Diego), gives it a unique take on a country so vast and full of contradictions. “I think we’re all outsiders to this version of America,” he says. “It doesn’t matter where you live … no one experiences the America that we’re portraying here in its fullness.”
What to play
One of the few games brave enough to release in the dead zone surrounding GTA VI is Tanuki: Pon’s Summer, a whimsical delight of a game about a chubby raccoon trying to rebuild the shrine he calls home. I played an earlier version at Tokyo game show a couple of years back, and am delighted to discover that it’s come out brilliantly. “Arriving alongside November’s blue wave, Tanuki: Pon’s Summer is a game of quiet restoration that feels perfectly suited to the current moment,” as writer Christian Donlan puts it in a review out this week. “Tasked with repairing an ancient shrine in the weeks leading up to a local festival, you’ll find yourself cleaning out trash, mending broken arches and slowly bringing a small rural community back together.”
Available on: Xbox (on Game Pass), Switch, PC
  
Estimated playtime: 
 six hours
What to read
- The brilliant cooperative indie darling Big Walk has become mired in AI controversy after the Independent games festival awards put out a statement on its stance about the use of large language models in nominated games. Out of what appears to be an abundance of caution, Big Walk’s House House developers disclosed to the IGF jurors that they used an LLM to help solve a coding problem during the game’s development. The fallout has illustrated how vociferous the anti-AI sentiment is among gaming creatives and has raised difficult questions about where to draw the line.
- Nintendo is hiring a historian/librarian to help preserve and document the creation of its games and hardware.
- A documentary film about the final years of legendary developer BioWare is coming, from Canada’s Super Channel. The studio was closed by EA last month after a 30-year run creating some of the most influential RPGs ever made.
What to click
- ‘It’s so glossy and sexy!’: 10 movies (and one TV show) that inspired Grand Theft Auto
- The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has revived the midnight game launch – but was it worth the wait?
- Crime pays: how Grand Theft Auto became a cultural colossus
Question Block
Please do keep sending in your questions and comments about GTA VI – next week’s issue will be a big Q&A about the game. In the meantime, reader Tim asks:
“I’m really worried about spoilers, to the point where I’m thinking of drawing up a joke contract for my son to sign so he agrees not to spoil it (teenagers these days just seem to blast through story mode, whereas I like to savour it). In a world where South Park contained Red Dead Redemption 2 spoilers, how the hell can we avoid them? Any tips??”
Honestly, you might be fighting a losing battle unless you a) stay off the internet entirely and b) speak to nobody at all in person who might possibly be playing it. GTA VI is a massive game that should, rightly, take weeks or months to work your way through, but we all know that a thousand content creators will have somehow gotten through the entire thing and put all of the footage on YouTube within days of its release.
The great thing about Rockstar games, though, is that outside of the story you really are creating your own experience, choosing what to do and how to spend your time, how your Jason and Lucia act. And nobody can spoil that for you.
If you have a question for Question Block – or anything else to say about the newsletter – hit reply or email us at pushingbuttons@theguardian.com.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Defesa Civil esclarece que kit de emergência é preventivo e não indica desastre iminente
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Marcela Brandes
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Uma publicação da Defesa Civil Nacional sobre a montagem de um kit de emergência para 72 horas provocou dúvidas e apreensão nas redes sociais ao longo do fim de semana. Parte dos usuários interpretou o conteúdo como indício de que alguma situação de risco estaria prestes a acontecer. Diante da repercussão, o órgão e o Ministério da Integração e do Desenvolvimento Regional, ao qual a Defesa Civil está vinculada, informaram que a orientação não se relaciona a nenhum alerta específico e tem caráter exclusivamente preventivo.
A primeira publicação foi feita na sexta-feira (6), quando a Defesa Civil Nacional incentivou os brasileiros a prepararem um kit de emergência como “uma atitude importante de prevenção”, já que, em desastres de grandes proporções, a ajuda pode demorar a chegar. Dois dias depois, no domingo (8), o órgão divulgou uma segunda postagem para responder aos questionamentos. “Calma! Falar de kit de emergência não é sinal de perigo, é sinal de que prevenir faz parte da rotina”, diz a legenda, que pede que não se crie pânico.
A própria Defesa Civil Nacional respondeu a comentários dizendo que se tratava apenas de conteúdo educativo e, na segunda publicação, usou um tom bem-humorado para reforçar que falar em kit de emergência não significa que exista algum perigo previsto.
A nota do ministério
Na noite de sábado (7), o ministério divulgou nota em que afirma que a recomendação “não está relacionada a qualquer alerta nacional ou a uma previsão de interrupção generalizada nos serviços públicos ou de abastecimento”. A pasta explicou que a Secretaria Nacional de Proteção e Defesa Civil divulga regularmente orientações gerais de autoproteção para diferentes situações de emergência e desastres, incluindo recomendações sobre como agir em vários cenários de risco.
O ministério também informou que o material não era inédito. Orientações semelhantes já haviam sido publicadas nas redes da Defesa Civil Nacional em 16 e 29 de março e em 3 de abril deste ano.
O que significam as 72 horas
A menção ao período de três dias foi um dos pontos que mais geraram confusão. De acordo com a Defesa Civil Nacional, as 72 horas correspondem à autonomia que os itens do kit devem garantir a cada família em uma eventual emergência. Não se trata, portanto, de uma previsão de que o kit será necessário nos três dias seguintes à publicação.
O órgão explica que a proposta é assegurar condições básicas de sobrevivência enquanto as equipes de socorro atuam. Em desastres de grande proporção, a dificuldade de acesso a determinadas localidades pode atrasar o atendimento, e a preparação antecipada permite que os moradores tenham recursos essenciais à mão até que a assistência chegue e os serviços sejam restabelecidos.
O que deve ter na mochila
A recomendação é montar uma mochila com itens suficientes para atender às necessidades básicas de cada integrante da família por 72 horas. De acordo com a orientação divulgada, isso inclui dois litros de água potável por dia para cada pessoa, alimentos não perecíveis, como enlatados e frutas secas, medicamentos de uso contínuo e de emergência, materiais de primeiros socorros e produtos de higiene pessoal.
A lista traz ainda roupas, calçados confortáveis, lanterna, pilhas, rádio, carregador de celular, bateria portátil e documentos pessoais protegidos em embalagem impermeável. Famílias com crianças, bebês ou animais de estimação devem acrescentar os itens específicos de cada um. A Defesa Civil orienta considerar as necessidades particulares dos moradores, manter os produtos dentro do prazo de validade e revisar o material periodicamente.
Reações nas redes
Nos comentários da publicação, houve quem perguntasse se as autoridades sabiam de algo que não havia sido divulgado. Outros ironizaram a possibilidade de um apocalipse. “Será que está caindo um meteoro na Terra e ninguém falou nada?”, escreveu um usuário. A Agência Brasil registra que muitos comentários classificaram a iniciativa como “exagero”, enquanto outras pessoas compartilharam o receio de que algum desastre estivesse próximo.
Também houve quem afirmasse já conhecer a orientação. “Campanha preventiva da Defesa Civil, galera. É divulgada regularmente. A última foi no dia 03/04. Tá no feed”, comentou uma pessoa. Outra disse ensinar sobre preparação para emergências na internet há cinco anos. Um terceiro grupo defendeu a iniciativa: “Temos que ter essa cultura de prevenção como em outros países. Com calma e organização”, escreveu uma usuária, que contou já manter em casa uma reserva de alimentos, água e medicamentos. Outro usuário destacou que a preparação antecipada ajuda a reduzir os impactos de situações adversas.
Orientação também circula no Rio Grande do Sul
A Defesa Civil do Rio Grande do Sul também se manifestou e afirmou que “prevenção não é previsão, mas preparação”. Segundo o órgão estadual, as orientações sobre mochilas de emergência e armazenamento de alimentos fazem parte de um trabalho permanente de proteção da população. A instituição lembrou que já tratava do assunto em fevereiro, na série educativa “Defesa Civil de A a Z”, cuja letra K foi dedicada ao kit de emergência.
A Defesa Civil estadual destaca que a preparação deve começar dentro de casa, com atitudes simples, e ressalta que estar preparado não significa viver com medo, mas adotar medidas para proteger a família.
Chuvas e tornados no Sul
Embora não associe o kit a nenhum desastre específico ou iminente, o ministério informou que acompanha de perto as condições meteorológicas na região Sul, onde chuvas e alagamentos têm causado estragos. Na região, foi registrada a ocorrência de sete tornados, fenômenos com ventos que podem superar 100 quilômetros por hora.
Os temporais deixaram duas mortes confirmadas em Santa Catarina. No RS, outras duas mortes tinham a relação com as tempestades sob investigação. Para o fim de semana de 7 e 8 de novembro, o Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia havia emitido alerta vermelho para eventos climáticos extremos na região Sul.
Como receber os avisos
A Defesa Civil recomenda que a população acompanhe os alertas e as orientações dos órgãos estaduais e municipais, que levam em conta os riscos específicos de cada região. Para receber avisos da Defesa Civil por mensagem de texto, basta enviar o Código de Endereçamento Postal (CEP) da residência para o número 40199.

https://www.humanite.fr/monde/alimentati.title: Au Liban, plus d’un million de personnes en état d’insécurité alimentaire aiguë
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/alimentati.author: La rédaction avec AFP
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/alimentati.text:
Plus d’un million de personnes sont confrontées à une insécurité alimentaire aiguë au Liban, ont alerté ce mercredi 11 novembre des agences de l’ONU, appelant à une « action urgente » pour y remédier.
« Plus d’un million de personnes sont confrontées à une insécurité alimentaire aiguë. Ce chiffre devrait atteindre 1,15 million d’ici à la mi-2027 », soit près du quart de la population libanaise, alerte un communiqué conjoint de l’Organisation des Nations unies pour l’alimentation et l’agriculture (FAO), du Programme Alimentaire Mondial (PAM) et du ministère libanais de l’Agriculture.
Le pays a connu deux guerres successives avec Israël alors qu’il est toujours englué dans une crise économique sans précédent depuis plus de sept ans. En découlent de graves conséquences.
« Les possibilités d’emploi restent limitées, les économies des ménages ont été épuisées et leur endettement demeure élevé, tandis que le coût de l’alimentation, du carburant et des autres produits de première nécessité continue de peser sur les budgets des familles », souligne le communiqué.
Plus d’un million de déplacés depuis mars
La situation « nécessite une action urgente » et « demeure particulièrement préoccupante dans les zones touchées par le conflit dans le Sud », ainsi que dans des régions déshéritées du nord et de l’est du pays. Les autorités libanaises estiment que le coût de deux guerres menées par Israël contre le Hezbollah pro-iranien depuis octobre 2023 s’élève à environ 27 milliards de dollars.
La dernière guerre, déclenchée en mars en soutien à l’Iran, a fait plus d’un million de déplacés. Leur nombre est retombé à environ 300 000 depuis une baisse des violences en juin. Les guerres sont intervenues alors que le Liban, qui a connu un effondrement économique sans précédent en 2019, n’a toujours pas mené les réformes exigées par le Fonds monétaire international pour enclencher un plan d’aide au pays.
Être le journal de la paix, notre défi quotidien
Depuis Jaurès, la défense de la paix est dans notre ADN.
- Qui informe encore aujourd’hui sur les actions des pacifistes pour le désarmement ?
- Combien de médias rappellent que les combats de décolonisation ont encore cours, et qu’ils doivent être soutenus ?
- Combien valorisent les solidarités internationales, et s’engagent sans ambiguïté aux côtés des exilés ?
Nos valeurs n’ont pas de frontières.
Aidez-nous à soutenir le droit à l’autodétermination et l’option de la paix.
Je veux en savoir plus !
