https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
China says US ‘fabricating’ Nvidia spy claims to justify tech ‘blockade’
Nvidia CEO is under investigation for an affair with a woman whom US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy.
China has urged the United States to stop “fabricating so-called spy narratives and using them as a pretext for imposing a technological blockade”, amid national security concerns that emerged over an affair involving Nvidia’s CEO.
Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning made the comments at a press briefing on Thursday when asked about allegations that the woman with whom Nvidia’s Jensen Huang had a relationship was a Chinese spy.
Mao said that China’s scientific and technological progress was driven by independent innovation and open cooperation, adding that Beijing was willing to work with the US to implement a consensus reached by their two heads of state. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed to ease tariffs and lift restrictions on tech to de-escalate tensions following tit-for-tat tariffs in a trade deal in Busan, South Korea.
The remarks come ahead of a meeting next week between Trump and Xi at the APEC gathering in Shenzhen, southern China.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and turned it into the world’s leading supplier of the chips that power artificial intelligence (AI), has admitted to having an extramarital affair. The woman was reported to be Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed who US officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence.
Megaspeed on Thursday said it takes compliance obligations under US export control laws “extremely seriously” and that it “is committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government”.
Nvidia’s 63-year-old boss has spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced chips to China. Last year Trump cleared Nvidia’s H200 chips for export to China despite objections from Republicans and Democrats who fear Chinese dominance in AI technology.
China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denied the claims, calling them “entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China”.
Huang’s position at the top of the $4.2 trillion company hangs in the balance after Nvidia launched an investigation into him on Sunday. It is unclear whether the tech giant has a succession plan.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120382.title: Bundeshaushalt | Stromsteuer für Privathaushalte wird nicht gesenkt
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120382.text:
- Politik
- Bundeshaushalt
Stromsteuer für Privathaushalte wird nicht gesenkt
Die Koalition einigt sich bei den Etatverhandlungen auf Änderungen beim Wohngeld und Kindersofortzuschlag. Die geplante Plastiksteuer wird ausgesetzt.
Berlin. Die von Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) angestrebte Senkung der Stromsteuer für Privathaushalte steht bei den Haushaltsverhandlungen der schwarz-roten Koalition weiter auf der Kippe. Bislang fehlt eine Gegenfinanzierung für die benötigten 5,4 Milliarden Euro. Union und SPD konnten zwar mehrere Streitpunkte ausräumen, müssen aber bis zu den abschließenden Beratungen im Haushaltsausschuss am Donnerstag weitere Kompromisse finden.
Einigen konnten sich die Koalitionspartner am Mittwochabend dagegen bei mehreren geplanten Steuern. Eine Abgabe auf Plastikverpackungen soll 2027 nicht erhoben werden. Die Zuckersteuer auf stark gesüßte Getränke wird auf den 1. Januar 2028 verschoben. Eine Erhöhung der Schaumweinsteuer ist ebenfalls vom Tisch. Im Gegenzug soll unter anderem der Personalabbau in der Bundesverwaltung verstärkt werden.
Kompromisse bei sozialen Kürzungen
Bei den Sozialleistungen gab es Zugeständnisse an die SPD. Geplante Kürzungen beim Kindersofortzuschlag für einkommensschwache Familien sollen weitgehend entfallen. Ausgenommen sind Asylbewerber. Über Änderungen beim Unterhaltsvorschuss und Elterngeld wird noch verhandelt. Die für 2027 vorgesehene Erhöhung des Wohngeldes soll ausgesetzt werden, der grundsätzliche Leistungsumfang aber erhalten bleiben.
Bei weiteren Entlastungen angesichts hoher Energiepreise gehen die Vorstellungen auseinander. Während die Union die Stromsteuersenkung zur Priorität erklärt, setzt die SPD vor allem auf einen Spritpreisdeckel, der den Staat kein zusätzliches Geld kosten soll. Eine Lösung könnte im Koalitionsausschuss am kommenden Dienstag gesucht werden.
CDU für Ausgleich der kalten Progression
Die Union hält zudem an einem vollständigen Ausgleich der sogenannten kalten Progression bei der Einkommensteuer fest. Diese entsteht, wenn inflationsbedingte Lohnerhöhungen zu einer höheren Steuerbelastung führen, ohne dass die Kaufkraft steigt. Die Entlastung würde Bund, Länder und Kommunen rund 4,2 Milliarden Euro kosten. Eine rückwirkende Umsetzung sei ebenfalls denkbar, falls zunächst keine Finanzierung gefunden werde.
Die geplante Einkommensteuerreform von Finanzminister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) soll Anfang 2027 in Kraft treten. Ab 2028 sind jährliche Entlastungen von insgesamt zehn Milliarden Euro vorgesehen. Profitieren sollen vor allem kleine und mittlere Einkommen sowie Familien. dpa/nd
Kein Milliardär im Rücken

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Após denúncia do MPSP, ‘é preciso uma reestruturação total do sistema de transporte de São Paulo’, afirma Nabil Bonduki
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Larissa Bohrer
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O ex-vereador e ex-presidente da Câmara Municipal Milton Leite (União Brasil) foi denunciado pelo Ministério Público de São Paulo (MP-SP) por trabalhar pelos interesses do Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) no sistema de transporte público da capital paulista e cidades da região. Também foi denunciado o ex-presidente da SPTrans da gestão Ricardo Nunes (MDB), Levi dos Santos Oliveira. Leite está preso desde o dia 18 de setembro.
A investigação aponta que Leite seria o verdadeiro dono da empresa Transwolff, que atuou em linhas de ônibus da capital paulista, e que os sócios dela estariam subordinados ao ex-vereador. Sua defesa afirmou que está tomando conhecimento da denúncia e, por enquanto, não irá se manifestar.
Ao Conexão BdF, da Rádio Brasil de Fato, o vereador Nabil Bonduki (PT) afirma que o transporte coletivo de São Paulo precisa ser totalmente reestruturado. Atualmente, segundo Bonduki, o sistema é caro e não oferece qualidade. “É um sistema que consome quase R$ 6 bilhões do orçamento municipal, embora seja cobrada tarifa e o serviço tem caído de qualidade de forma muito acentuada”, afirma, ao mencionar redução de linhas.
“Leite exerceu uma influência muito grande e durante muito tempo sobre esse sistema, indicando secretários, presidentes das empresas”, avalia.
Bonduki ressalta que não comentará o eventual elo de Leite e dessa máfia dos transportes com o crime organizado, mas que o mais importante é compreender que o sistema precisa ser repensado. Um dos problemas apontados pelo vereador é a concessão de 20 anos. “É totalmente inadequado, porque o sistema não está bem”, afirma.
Na avaliação do vereador, uma das urgências é realizar uma reestruturação das linhas da cidade. “Nós temos linhas ociosas e faltas de ônibus. Tem falta de ônibus em algumas regiões da cidade e ônibus ociosos em outras. O contrato de concessão precisaria ser revisto”, defende, ao também citar a necessidade de abrir nova licitação para que outras empresas possam concorrer. “Hoje a gente tem um cartel na cidade de São Paulo. É um sistema em crise e que não atende aos passageiros, inclusive vem perdendo passageiros porque o sistema é ruim”, afirma.
Para ouvir e assistir
O jornal Conexão BdF vai ao ar em duas edições, de segunda a sexta-feira: a primeira às 12h e a segunda às 17h, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM, na Grande São Paulo, com transmissão simultânea também pelo YouTube do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/slow-.title: ‘A slow genocide accelerated’: How Gaza’s winter ‘crisis’ is manufactured by Israel
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/slow-.author: Katherine Hearst
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/slow-.text:
‘A slow genocide accelerated’: How Gaza’s winter ‘crisis’ is manufactured by Israel
Days ago, baby Ehab Mohammad Hamad was found by his mother, lifeless with blue lips, fingers and toes.
The six-month year old died of exposure after his family’s tent was flooded.
“No matter how hard we tried to keep the child warm and wrap him in blankets, it was all in vain,” the child’s grandmother said in a video posted by the Palestinian-led mutual aid group, the Sameer Project.
The group provided the family with a dome tent. But Hala Sabbah, who works with the organisation, said that the story fell on deaf ears.
“I was really frustrated that it wasn’t talked about,” Sabbah told MEE.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
The deaths of Gaza’s babies in freezing, storm-battered tents is now becoming an annual phenomenon in the aid-starved enclave.
For the fourth winter in a row, rains have swept through Gaza, exposing woefully inadequate supplies of materials for shelter entering the strip.
“There are tens of thousands of tents, winter coats, blankets, pallets and pallets, truckloads full of these things that are simply waiting in warehouses'
- Sean Jones, Unwra
This has forced 65 percent of the population - around 1.4m people - to shelter in makeshift shelters or tents which have been swamped in the downpour, or damaged buildings which risk collapse.
While the weather is turbocharged by a strengthening El Nino event, the paucity of aid is entirely man-made, leveraged as a pressure point by Israel over Gaza’s population.
The Israeli authorities have long restricted the entry of shelter and construction materials into Gaza, with vital equipment like tent poles and mobile homes deemed to be “dual use”.
On Sunday, the UN aid coordination office (Ocha) confirmed that 150,000 tents are prepositioned outside Gaza waiting to be delivered.
“There are tens of thousands of tents, winter coats, blankets, pallets and pallets, truckloads full of these things that are simply waiting in warehouses because they've not received normal approvals by the Israelis to let them in,” Sean Jones, director of the UN agency for Palestinian refugees (Unrwa) in Gaza told MEE.
“It's part of the trend line we see, a concerted effort just to delay,” he added.
Part of the plan
But in recent months, even fewer pallets of shelter aid appear to be struggling across the border. According to the Palestine Shelter Cluster, the number of trucks carrying shelter and household items into Gaza plummeted from 908 in December 2025, to 409 in January 2026.
In October, weeks before the storm struck, just nine percent of aid trucks that entered that month carried shelter items.
With the Rafah crossing closed to aid in May, minimal numbers of trucks trickle through the Kerem Shalom crossing, the only route into the territory open to aid.
'This is part of Israel's plan - to push us out, to not let us bring in the aid that we need in order to respond to people'
- Shaina Low, Norwegian Refugee Council
The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) reported in early October that the authorities were allowing just 15 trucks carrying dual-use items in one day per week.
It warned that at the current rate of entry of dual-use items, in a best-case scenario it would take seven months for the winter aid stored in warehouses outside the strip to enter.
An assessment of shelter needs in Gaza by the Shelter Cluster in August this year revealed that an estimated 1.98 million people, 94 percent of the population, were classified in Shelter Severity Phases 3 (Crisis), 4 (Critical), or 5 (Catastrophic).
It showed that only 10 percent of those surveyed received shelter aid in the month prior to the data collection.
While the needs in Gaza are enormous, humanitarian groups are hamstrung.
In December last year, Israel banned 37 international NGOs, including the NRC, Medecins Sans Frontieres and Oxfam, from operating in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
While the ban was subject to a temporary injunction, it is still in effect, barring the groups from bringing aid and international staff into the territory.
This and the ban issued against Unrwa - previously the main heavy lifter in terms of shelter provision in Gaza - has meant the majority of shelter aid is brought in bilaterally through committees run by the Egyptian, Qatari, Emirati and Saudi governments.
“The stockpiles inside of Gaza from INGOs are extremely low,” Shaina Low, the NRC’s communication adviser in Palestine, told MEE.
“This is part of Israel's plan to push us out, to not let us bring in the aid that we need in order to respond to people. And so the committees are the ones that seem to be able to get more aid in.”
Not fit for purpose
Due to the reduced footprint of international NGOs on the ground in Gaza, small Palestinian-led mutual aid groups like the Sameer Project have stepped into the void to buy tents on the market and distribute them.
But scarcity has sent prices soaring. According to the Shelter Cluster, the cost of tents has rocketed by 52 percent, costing $655, while emergency shelter kits have soared by 1,233 percent to $4000.
'There had been a slow genocide throughout 2026, but over the last three to four months, we're seeing acceleration, and this is a part of their strategy'
- Hala Sabbah, Sameer Project
“A lot of tents that come in are stolen and sold on the market,” Sabbah told MEE, adding that tents are distributed to people on lists approved by the Israeli authorities.
“It’s a whole system that’s designed, you have people who are living in homes being allocated tents,” she said.
The quality of the tents has also deteriorated, as Palestinians are forced to reuse old materials.
According to the Shelter Cluster’s August assessment, over 50 percent of Palestinians sheltering in tents are using ones that are in poor or very poor condition. Fifty-four percent of them are using tents or makeshift shelters that they've been in for a year or more.
“These are materials that only last a few months. The lifespan is really short, especially with the weather conditions in Gaza, and so people are just living in really, really difficult circumstances without access to materials to improve their living conditions,” Low said.
“We're still seeing that supplies that are entering are not necessarily fit for purpose,” she added. “Not all tents are water resistant, which means we need to divert resources like tarpaulins to reinforce them.”
According to Sabbah, many of the tents that are making it over the border appear to be made of an inferior material to previous years and are not water resistant, and require two tarpaulins to be layered over them.
Inseparable from genocide
While Palestinians in Gaza have already endured three winters in threadbare tents, this year, due to the razing of buildings and infrastructure by Israel, they are forced to camp on ever-smaller patches of land.
A spatial analysis by Forensic Architecture revealed that, over the course of the genocide, Gaza’s displaced population has increasingly been forced into low-lying areas on Gaza’s coast.
As Israel’s expanding "yellow line" swallows up more of the territory, and the fact that much of the land is coated in debris means that they have nowhere else to go.
“The tent camps now flooding are not an incidental feature of this,” Nicola Banks, Forensic Architecture's head of communications, told MEE.
“They occupy the very spaces into which Palestinians have been forcibly concentrated, often on land without the infrastructure needed to sustain life,” she said.
“The floods make visible what our investigation traces spatially, that the destruction of Gaza's built environment and the material conditions of Palestinian existence are inseparable from the ongoing genocide.”
Sabbah said that this year, the team she works with in Gaza are already exhausted, their bodies worn out by the demands of the previous three winters.
“People are taking much more sick leave than they used to in the past,” she said.
“Their bodies are depleted. It's one thing to face winter in genocide when you're a young healthy man versus someone who has lived in these conditions for four years.
“There had been a slow genocide throughout 2026, but over the last three to four months, we're seeing acceleration, and I think this is a part of their strategy,” Sabbah told MEE.
“They're not doing something very intense all at once because they don't want backlash from their international community.
“Its a slow genocide, accelerated.”

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.title: Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in Gaza kills surgeon and five others
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.author: Seham Tantesh in Gaza and William Christou in Beirut
https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/n.text:
An Israeli airstrike on Nasser hospital in southern Gaza killed six people, including a surgeon and a disabled man, and wounded more than 20 others, the Palestinian news agency reported.
The Israeli military carried out the attack on the hospital, in Khan Younis, early on Thursday saying in a statement it had struck a Hamas commander and other fighters there, without providing evidence.
The strike destroyed part of the surgery department, and caused extensive damage to several floors. Videos showed smoke filling rubble-strewn hallways, with medical equipment broken and knocked over from the blast.
“The bombing caused thick smoke to fill the rooms and fires to break out, amid the groans of wounded and people’s screams. There were many casualties and blood everywhere … Most of us sustained injuries to our limbs, as well as shrapnel wounds in different parts of our bodies,” said Dr Ayman Abu Ubaid, a surgical specialist at Nasser medical complex who was wounded in the attack.
Ubaid said the strike happened at about 12.30am, without warning. “The patients in the department were all surgical patients waiting to undergo operations. The bombing happened at a time when they should have been asleep,” he said.
Among the dead was Rizk Abu Shaira, a general surgeon who had been featured in a documentary about doctors operating in Gaza, called American Doctor.
“Dr Rizk was in the American Doctor documentary operating and serving his people. He lost his life doing that, he lost his life because he was doing that,” Dr Thaer Ahmad, who also featured in the documentary, posted on X.
Nasser hospital is one of the last functioning healthcare facilities in Gaza after Israeli bombing made most of the strip’s facilities unusable. Israel also struck the hospital last year, killing five journalists in a double-tap strike on a location often used by reporters for filming.
The Israeli military has accused Hamas of using hospitals as command centres and to store weapons, an accusation the militant movement rejects. More than 1,700 healthcare workers have been killed in Gaza, while Israel has detained hundreds of medics since 7 October 2023, with at least 95 still in custody, according to Doctors Without Borders (MSF).
About 90% of Gaza’s health infrastructure has been destroyed or damage by Israeli bombing, systematic destruction UN experts called “medicide”.
Attacking healthcare facilities and staff is illegal under international humanitarian law, though facilities can lose their protected status if they are used for military purposes.
There is an increased need for healthcare during the winter months in Gaza, where rains have displaced people from their tents and increased communicable diseases in crowded encampments.
One of those killed in Thursday’s strike was Seif Ghazi Abu Hatab, 29, who had checked in to Nasser hospital on Monday after a piece of debris fell on his back while he was helping clear rubble from a friend’s home. He was scheduled for surgery at 10am on Thursday, and was meant to receive further treatment abroad.
“Seif was a young man in the prime of his life. He wanted to live, rebuild his home and start a normal life, free from problems and suffering … Seif was killed after already losing two of his brothers and his father. His mother has now lost three of her sons,” said his cousin Tareq Abu Hatab, 37.
Israel launched the war in Gaza after the 7 October 2023 Hamas-led attack that killed about 1,200 people and took 251 hostage. At least 74,645 people have since been killed in Gaza and Israel has carried out a genocide in the strip, according to the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
Israel continues to carry out airstrikes in Gaza, killing more than 1,600 people since the October 2025 “ceasefire” according to the Gaza ministry of health.

https://taz.de/Longevity-Lifestyle-Prote.title: Longevity als Geschäftsmodell: Proteine und Krafttraining sind nicht der Sinn des Lebens
https://taz.de/Longevity-Lifestyle-Prote.author: Simone Dede Ayivi
https://taz.de/Longevity-Lifestyle-Prote.text:
Longevity als Geschäftsmodell: Proteine und Krafttraining sind nicht der Sinn des Lebens
Die Beauty-, Fitness- und Lebensmittelindustrie verspricht uns, langsamer zu altern. Doch was will ich mit einem langen Leben, wenn es kein süßes ist?
N ach „alt“ kommt „tot“. Das ist so unausweichlich wie belastend. Klar beschäftigt mich mein eigenes Altern. Sonst wüsste ich nicht, was eine Nasolabialfalte ist. Und doch überrascht es mich, dass altern immer weniger als Teil des Lebens betrachtet wird, sondern als ein Problem, das mit viel Disziplin gelöst werden muss. Weil niemand diszipliniert genug sein kann, um den Alterungsprozess zu stoppen oder gar zurückzudrehen, sind nicht wenige dazu bereit, Geld auf dieses Problem zu schmeißen. Longevity und Anti-Aging sind dabei zwei Seiten der gleichen Selbstoptimierungsmedaille.
Altern als Geschäftsmodell, das ist eine unternehmerisch starke Idee. Denn altern tun wir fast alle, und wer nicht mehr altert, der kann ohnehin nichts mehr kaufen. Es ist so traurig wie nachvollziehbar, dass das Nachdenken über die Endlichkeit des Lebens und Sorgen um den Körper unsere Geldbeutel öffnen. Dabei geht es nur oberflächlich um Gesundheit und Schönheit. Es geht um Kontrolle, die es jedoch nicht geben kann.
Umso mehr verachte ich Beauty- und Fitnessindustrie, Schönheitschirurgen und Nahrungsergänzungsmittelhersteller, die diese Ängste befeuern, um damit Kasse zu machen, und gleichzeitig dazu beitragen, dass Gesundheit im Alter zur individuellen Verantwortung und Lebensentscheidung erklärt wird. Wobei die Empfehlung für Langlebigkeit stets lautet, nach Feierabend den Arsch hochzukriegen. Forderungen nach Verkürzung der Arbeitszeit, Entlastung bei Sorgearbeit, Verbesserung der Gesundheitsversorgung oder ein früheres Renteneintrittsalter, besonders für Menschen in körperlich und seelisch belastenden Berufen, findet man weder unter dem Schlagwort „Anti-Aging“ noch unter „Longevity“.
Das Leben macht nur Sinn, wenn es Spaß macht
Diese Gesellschaft altert und ist gleichzeitig alters- und behindertenfeindlich. Die Folgen des demografischen Wandels werden an den Einzelnen ausgelagert. Es wird nicht lange dauern, bis in Diskussionen um die Pflegekrise zu hören sein wird, Pflegebedürftige seien selbst schuld. Wer mit 90 nicht mehr für sich sorgen kann, dürfe nicht durch Unterstützung auch noch dafür belohnt werden, sein Krafttraining vernachlässigt zu haben. Gesundheit und Jugendlichkeit gilt zudem als Statussymbol. Sport ist gesund, aber Gesundheit als Sport ist ableistischer Bullshit, denn wer aus Gesundheit einen Wettbewerb macht, belegt Krankheit noch mehr mit Scham, als es ohnehin der Fall ist.
Ein gesundes, langes Leben erfüllt nur dann seinen Sinn, wenn es auch Spaß macht. Ein kohlenhydrat- und partyfreies Leben ist genauso ausdruckslos wie diese Botoxgesichter. Es wird sich am Ende nicht anfühlen, als wäre man lange auf diesem Planeten gewesen, wenn man seine Zeit nur damit verbracht haben, das eigene Dasein zu verlängern. Proteine und Krafttraining sind nicht der Sinn des Lebens. Retinoide und Kollagen-Booster sind keine Investition. Viele können sich das lange Leben wohl noch nicht einmal leisten: Sonst würden sie nicht ständig über ETF-Sparpläne reden.
Mein Körper ist kein Projekt. Und ich habe keine Lust, meine begrenzte Lebenszeit mit langweiligen Leuten zu verbringen, deren Projekt ihr Körper ist. Ein längeres Leben fände ich nur erstrebenswert, wenn es ein süßes Leben ist. Was soll ich mit zusätzlichen Jahren anfangen, wenn sie mit Zuckerfreiheit erkauft wurden?

Damit wir auch morgen noch unseren Journalismus machen können, brauchen wir mehr Unterstützung für taz zahl ich. Dank Ihnen haben wir nun die 50.000 erreicht. https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: Manchester United sack Michael Carrick as manager
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Manchester United sack Michael Carrick as manager
Carrick exits after United drop to 18th in Premier League table; he led them to three wins across all competitions.
Manchester United have sacked manager Michael Carrick, the Premier League club confirmed in a statement, amid a torrid time for the global football giants, who find themselves in the league’s relegation zone.
Carrick’s departure, which had been imminent after United made their worst start to the English top flight in 40 years, was announced on Thursday by the club, which said it would “appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible”.
“Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach”, the Old Trafford club said in a statement.
“After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.”
United, 13-time Premier League champions, have been heavily linked with US Men’s National Team coach Mauricio Pochettino.
Pochettino – whose release from the contract extension he signed as USA head coach has reportedly been arranged – would become the eighth permanent man in charge at Old Trafford since Sir Alex Ferguson’s departure in May 2013 after more than 26 years in the job.
United’s statement termed Carrick a club legend.
“Just as he [Carrick] did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club,” the statement added.
“His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.”
The 45-year-old’s last game as United’s head coach ended in a dramatic late draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford, where the furious home fans voiced their anger towards the club’s ownership.
United needed a stoppage-time equaliser to eke out a point against 10th-placed Villa, but it was not enough to lift them out of the Premier League’s relegation zone.
The Red Devils briefly dropped to the bottom of the table before results elsewhere in the league took them back to 18th place with eight points from their 10 games this season.
Carrick, who was handed the United job on an interim basis in January, knew his managerial position was under threat following a series of disappointing results in recent weeks.
United have endured four losses and five draws, with their solitary win coming against Ipswich Town in late August.
They were also knocked out of the English League Cup in the third round, and have made an unconvincing start in their Champions League campaign, with two wins and as many losses.
Overall, United have won only three times in 15 games across all competitions this season.
Carrick’s sacking marks the end of a rollercoaster reign at the club.
The former United midfielder, who also captained the club in his final season as a player, took over from the sacked Ruben Amorim last term, when the team were seventh, but lifted them to a third-place finish and secured Champions League qualification at the end of the 2025-26 season.
The players looked like a better, more exciting version of themselves under Carrick when he first took over, but fans’ optimism vanished when the revival did not continue into the current campaign.
United’s defeat to newly-promoted Hull City in their opening match of the league season marked an embarrassing start for the former champions. What followed was further humiliation on and off the field, with a dressing room rift damaging Carrick’s image, and the club’s hierarchy losing faith in one of their own.
British media have linked several high-profile managers to the job.
Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann were among the frontrunners, but USA men’s national team coach Mauricio Pochettino has seemingly overtaken both as favourite.
Pochettino, who previously took charge of Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the English top flight, has been widely favoured by US and British media.
Former Chelsea coach Antonio Conte is also in the running.
A managerial change is expected during this international break, with a new face likely to lead United on their trip to Anfield to face longtime rivals, Liverpool, on November 22.

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120382.title: Soziale Krise | Spanien: Protest gegen Wohnungsnot und steigenden Preisen hält an
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120382.text:
- Politik
- Soziale Krise
Spanien: Protest gegen Wohnungsnot und steigenden Preisen hält an
Der Generalstreik in Spanien endete mit großen Demonstrationen in Madrid und Barcelona. Hunderttausende gingen landesweit auf die Straße.
Madrid. Nach Kundgebungen gegen die Wohnungsnot und steigende Preise in Madrid und Barcelona kam es in beiden Städten zu Zwischenfällen. Demonstrierende und Polizisten gerieten nach den Protestzügen am Mittwoch aneinander. Die Polizei setzte nach Angaben von AFP-Reportern Gummigeschosse und Tränengas ein, um kleine Gruppen von Demonstranten auseinanderzutreiben, die Müllcontainer in Brand setzten und mit Gegenständen warfen.
Angesichts der Wohnungskrise und der steigenden Preise hatten am Mittwoch in Madrid nach Angaben der Behörden rund 120.000 Menschen protestiert. Die Demonstration im Zentrum der spanischen Hauptstadt bildete den Abschluss eines landesweiten Generalstreiks. In Barcelona gingen nach Angaben der Stadtpolizei rund 55.000 Menschen auf die Straße.
Die Wohnungskrise ist seit Jahren eines der drängendsten sozialen Probleme Spaniens. Immer weiter steigende Mieten können viele Menschen nicht mehr bezahlen. Die Gewerkschaften fordern unter anderem den Bau von 1,5 Millionen Sozialwohnungen in den kommenden Jahren und ein Verbot der Zwangsräumung schutzbedürftiger Mieter.
Auslöser der jüngsten Protestwelle war die Zwangsräumung einer 87-jährigen Rentnerin in Madrid im September. Sie starb wenige Tage später.
Ein Streit um von der Regierung vorgeschlagene Maßnahmen für mehr Mieterschutz führte letztlich dazu, dass der linksgerichtete Regierungschef Pedro Sánchez Neuwahlen für den 29. November ausrief. Der seit 2018 regierende Sánchez unterstützt die Protestbewegung, steht wegen der Wohnungspolitik aber auch in der Kritik. Umfragen zufolge liegen die Konservativen und Rechtsextremen derzeit in der Wählergunst vorne. Die konservative Volkspartei und die rechtsextreme Vox-Partei lehnen den Streik ab. AFP/nd
Ohne dich geht die Rechnung nicht auf
Bei uns muss niemand zahlen, um informiert zu sein. Klingt nach einem schlechten Geschäftsmodell? Ist es auch. Aber uns sind unabhängiger Journalismus und Teilhabe für alle wichtiger als Profit. Journalismus kostet trotzdem Geld: Recherche, Druck und all die Menschen, die ihn machen. Deshalb sind wir auf dich angewiesen. Bis Ende des Jahres brauchen wir 300.000 Euro.
Spende einmalig oder regelmäßig, jeder Betrag zählt. Damit nd bleibt.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Farsa do triplex elegeu Bolsonaro, enquanto Lula segue com injusto rótulo de corrupto, avalia cientista política
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Larissa Bohrer
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Passados mais de dez anos da deflagração da Operação Lava Jato, que, entre as muitas consequências, colocou Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) na cadeia por 580 dias por causa de um triplex no Guarujá, litoral sul paulista, a Justiça reconheceu que o apartamento nunca pertenceu ao presidente. O imóvel pertence à OAS Empreendimentos, que, conforme determinação da Justiça Federal, vai receber os valores provenientes do leilão.
A farsa jurídica em que se transformou a operação liderada pelo então juiz, hoje senador e governador eleito do Paraná, Sérgio Moro (PL), tirou Lula da disputa presidencial em 2018 abrindo caminho para a eleição de Jair Bolsonaro.
A cientista política Larissa Peixoto, pesquisadora na Universidade de Edimburgo, avalia que, até hoje, a população brasileira não tem a dimensão dos impactos que a operação, que virou uma perseguição política, representou para a democracia. “A gente tem agora o resultado no papel do que a gente já sabia: o triplex nunca foi do Lula e o próprio Moro falava não ter evidências, o que é uma coisa insana”, ressalta ao Conexão BdF, da Rádio Brasil de Fato.
Peixoto, no entanto, destaca que as consequências disso foram sentidas por toda a população. “O [Jair] Bolsonaro foi eleito e 700 mil pessoas morreram por causa das decisões tomadas por ele, e o Lula é até hoje chamado de corrupto por causa do triplex”, afirma.
A cientista política lembra que a Lava Jato, originalmente, começou sob o governo Dilma Rousseff e que tinha o objetivo de combate à corrupção. Mas, após o golpe contra a presidenta e a chegada de Michel Temer ao poder, as dinâmicas mudaram completamente e a operação virou um palanque para promotores e juízes que viraram políticos. “Ela [a Lava Jato] perdeu o freio. Você tem um juiz de uma vara local virar ministro de Justiça; é evidente que tinham interesses políticos. Aquilo não pode ser considerada uma questão legal, mas uma questão política”, frisa.
Larissa Peixoto defende que, diante dos fatos, uma investigação sobre a conduta dos envolvidos na Lava Jato deveria ser feita. “Eu gostaria muito de ver alguma investigação. Foi um juiz agindo como um promotor. É um juiz fazendo investigação. Tinham mensagens entre Moro e Dallagnol. No mínimo, eles tinham que desaparecer da política”, afirma.
Para ouvir e assistir
O jornal Conexão BdF vai ao ar em duas edições, de segunda a sexta-feira: a primeira às 12h e a segunda às 17h, na Rádio Brasil de Fato, 98.9 FM, na Grande São Paulo, com transmissão simultânea também pelo YouTube do Brasil de Fato.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/opinion/je.title: In the West, Jewish voices are embracing anti-Zionism. Palestinians must seize this moment
https://www.middleeasteye.net/opinion/je.author: Awad Abdelfattah
https://www.middleeasteye.net/opinion/je.text:
In the West, Jewish voices are embracing anti-Zionism. Palestinians must seize this moment
The publication of Benjamin Moser’s Anti-Zionism: A Jewish History comes at a significant political moment.
Alongside the growing anti-genocide movement in the West, and the British Green Party’s recent adoption of a motion supporting a single democratic state in historic Palestine, the book helps to bring a question once marginalised in mainstream western debate into sharper focus: is Zionism an inseparable expression of Jewish identity, or a political ideology that must itself be challenged?
Moser, an American Jewish writer and Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer, approaches this question by recovering a largely suppressed tradition of Jewish opposition to Zionism.
Through portraits of 12 Jewish figures, including Hannah Arendt, Edwin Montagu, Felicia Langer and Avi Shlaim, he demonstrates that opposition to Zionism is neither new nor alien to Jewish intellectual and political history.
The importance of his intervention goes beyond the historical recovery of individual voices. It challenges one of Zionism’s most powerful political claims: that Jewish identity, collective security and national existence necessarily require a state organised around Jewish privilege in Palestine.
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Moser’s work helps to establish that Jewish identity and opposition to Zionism are not contradictory, and that Jewish political and ethical traditions have also produced alternatives to exclusive nationalism.
This is particularly relevant after the genocide and destruction of Gaza, which have exposed the consequences of a political system founded on Palestinian dispossession, ethnic cleansing and the denial of Palestinian national rights.
Questioning Zionism
The growing willingness of Jewish intellectuals, activists and public figures to question Zionism has contributed to a wider shift in western political discourse.
The British Greens’ decision reflects this changing atmosphere. So does the mobilisation of Americans, Palestinians, Muslims, Jewish anti-Zionists, students, trade unionists and ordinary citizens who have challenged their governments’ military and political support for Israel.
What began, for many, as opposition to the destruction of Gaza has increasingly developed into a broader questioning of the structures of occupation, apartheid and settler-colonialism. Israel has become one of the most widely condemned countries in the world, and its founding myths are increasingly collapsing.
The central challenge is not simply to oppose Zionism, but to articulate and organise an alternative: a democratic political order in which Palestinians recover their rights
Yet an important distinction remains. Not everyone who opposes Israel’s actions supports anti-Zionism, and not everyone questioning Zionism has embraced the vision of one democratic state.
Nevertheless, the boundaries of political debate are changing. The question is no longer confined to how Palestinians might obtain a state alongside Israel, but increasingly concerns the legitimacy of the colonial Zionist project and the political framework that governs the entire territory, from the river to the sea.
Here lies an uncomfortable paradox for the Palestinian national movement. While sections of the western left are beginning to challenge Zionism as a political framework, much of the Palestinian leadership continues to negotiate within that framework, seeking a Palestinian state alongside Israel through a partition formula that has become increasingly detached from the realities on the ground.
This is not simply an intellectual disagreement. It concerns the future of the Palestinian liberation struggle.
International recognition of Palestinian statehood remains important and should not be dismissed. But recognition cannot be a substitute for the exercise of national rights, nor can it resolve questions about refugees, equality, dispossession and the fragmentation of the Palestinian people.
Right of return
The challenge is to move from a discussion around the “legitimacy” of partition to the legitimacy of rights. A single democratic state throughout historic Palestine - based on decolonisation, equal citizenship, collective rights and the right of return - offers a different political horizon.
It is not a merger of two existing states, or an arrangement that preserves colonial privilege. It requires dismantling the structures that prevent Palestinians and Israeli Jews from living together as equals.
The recent Israeli elections provided another perspective on this contradiction. Despite the continuing strength of the Zionist political consensus and ever-escalating colonial brutality, Palestinian citizens of Israel participated in unprecedented numbers.
Turnout in Arab localities reached approximately 80 percent, while Arab-led parties secured a combined 19 seats in the Knesset.
As a former head of the Balad party who advocated boycotting Israeli elections after the Knesset’s endorsement of the racist and colonial nation-state law in 2018, I regard this development as politically significant, but it must be interpreted carefully.
It would be a mistake to read this participation as an expression of confidence in Israeli democracy or acceptance of the Zionist state. Palestinians voted in circumstances of growing existential insecurity, political repression, narrowing of the public political space, state-sponsored organised crime, and escalating attacks on their communities.
For many, the ballot box remains one of the few available spaces through which they can defend their immediate interests, express their collective political identity, and resist the far right.
At the same time, these results expose the limitations of parliamentary politics. The increased electoral weight of Palestinian citizens has not removed the constitutional and institutional structures that deny them national equality. Nor can replacing one Israeli government with another, by itself, transform the political order.
Inseparable struggles
The deeper question is whether Palestinian participation can become part of a wider national project, rather than remaining confined to managing the consequences of colonial rule. Palestinians inside Israel cannot be reduced to a minority seeking better integration into the existing state.
Their struggle is inseparable from that of Palestinians in Gaza, the West Bank, Jerusalem, the refugee camps and the diaspora. Such an approach to the struggle and its political solution requires a radical shift in thinking, as well as an understanding that liberation is a long process that must be viewed in historical terms.
The contrast is striking. In parts of the western political arena, the legitimacy of Zionism itself is increasingly being questioned, and its lies exposed. Yet Palestinian political institutions remain largely trapped within the assumptions of the Oslo framework and the two-state paradigm.
This contradiction reflects years of political fragmentation, institutional stagnation and international pressure. But it also raises an urgent question about Palestinian political responsibility: Why should western progressive movements move beyond the political assumptions of partition, while Palestinians themselves remain hesitant to reconsider them?
Moser’s book and the British Greens’ decision do not offer Palestinians a ready-made political solution. Nor should the Palestinian future depend on western political parties or Jewish intellectuals.
Their significance lies in helping to open a political and intellectual space that Palestinians must now occupy with their own historical experience, political thinking and liberation project.
The task is to rebuild an inclusive Palestinian national movement, reconnect Palestinians across geographical and political divides, and transform the growing international solidarity movement into sustained political alliances.
Anti-Zionism without a democratic alternative and an agreed liberation vision and strategy remains incomplete. Equally, a one-state formula without decolonisation, equality and the right of return could reproduce domination under another name.
The central challenge, therefore, is not simply to oppose Zionism, but to articulate and organise an alternative: a democratic political order in which Palestinians recover their rights, and Israeli Jews - who will have to relinquish their colonial privileges - enjoy individual security, freedom and collective cultural rights, without the domination of one people over another.
The debate has begun to move beyond the legitimacy of partition. The Palestinian national movement must now confront the implications of this shift, and act in light of the dramatic changes taking place in American and European Jewish circles, as well as the evolving global solidarity movement struggling for justice and dignity.
The remarkable results of the American elections are opening up a new horizon, as the major supporter of the genocidal regime is in rapid decline, and the continued funding of crimes against humanity in Palestine and across our region is increasingly being questioned.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news-analysis/.title: From the UK to the Gulf, are US overseas bases becoming liabilities?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news-analysis/.text:
From the UK to the Gulf, are US overseas bases becoming liabilities?
For decades, these bases allowed the US to wage faraway wars and protect allies. Now, Iran has changed that calculation — for friends hosting these facilities, and for Washington.
Doha, Qatar — Late one morning in March 1999, a United States B-52 bomber took off from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, headed southeast. Seven more jets followed, at two-minute intervals.
It was the start of the US-led NATO bombing of Yugoslavia, a campaign in which the Fairford base served as both a pivotal launchpad for American jets and as a fuel station for fighter planes. The British base had served a similar role during the Gulf War in 1991, and would do so again during the 2003 Iraq war and in the early stages of the US-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28, 2026.
But in October, the US pulled all 12 of its B-1 Lancer bombers from the Gloucestershire base, amid fears that they were no longer safe there from a growing Iranian threat. Days earlier, British security forces had made several arrests, and the country’s government has accused Iran of being behind a plot to target the base — a charge Tehran has denied.
RAF Fairford is not alone. Earlier this month, the US withdrew a dozen planes from another British base, RAF Mildenhall. And in July, reports said that the US had relocated many of its military assets from its bases in the Gulf that were badly hit by Iran during the war, instead moving them to bases in Jordan, while also considering a proposal to shift them to Israel.
For decades, these bases have served as the sharp edge of the US military’s ability to project power and wage wars thousands of miles from home. For close allies, whether in Europe or the Gulf, they also worked as security guarantors against other threats.
But Iran’s ability to severely damage US facilities in the Middle East during the war, and pose a threat as far as the UK, has for the first time turned these critical strategic assets into potential liabilities, both for American allies and for the US itself, say analysts.
“The US security umbrella is becoming a double-edged sword,” Simon Mabon, a professor of international politics at Lancaster University, told Al Jazeera. “When the security of US bases is called into question, it changes Washington’s calculation of their strategic benefits. It also gives European and Gulf states reason to think seriously about the bases, given that they are becoming targets.”
How the Iran war changed the bargain
Hosting American bases has long been perceived as integral to how US allies, whether in Europe, the Gulf or East Asia, deter threats that they themselves face.
Former US President Barack Obama once spoke of an “ironclad commitment” to Gulf security, while Britain regularly invokes its so-called “special relationship” with the United States. In doing so, Britain and the Gulf have long cast themselves as willing partners to a power that — at least before current President Donald Trump — presented itself as the benevolent guarantor of its allies’ security.
But a spate of recent security incidents, many linked to the war on Iran, is testing that narrative and raising questions about whose interests these commitments serve, and whether hosting American forces could be bringing danger closer to home.
US prosecutors have charged three men they describe as Iranian-backed operatives over their alleged roles in plotting nearly 20 attacks across the United States and Europe, including on RAF Fairford.
Meanwhile, in the Gulf, Iran explicitly cited the presence of US bases as justification for targeting its neighbours, bombing Qatar, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and Kuwait. Iran also bombed Oman, which does not have a permanent US base; and Jordan and Iraq, beyond the Gulf, which do host major US military facilities.
A report by the Pentagon’s watchdog released in September revealed that Iranian attacks damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at US military installations in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Oman and Jordan in the first four months of the war.
At least five KC-135 aerial refuelling tankers were damaged when they were hit at the Prince Sultan airbase in Saudi Arabia. At least one of these airborne early-warning and control aircraft was damaged on the ground in a subsequent strike.
Experts say these incidents are sharpening a security dilemma for US allies in the Gulf and Europe. Hosting US forces can expose them to retaliation in a war they had no say in starting, while those same bases help defend some of those host countries from attacks, including by intercepting missiles and providing weapons transfers.
The war has disrupted flights and shipping, threatening the oil and gas exports on which much of the region depends. US President Donald Trump said on Monday that further military action against Iran was unnecessary for now. But the US naval blockade remains in place, and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has yet to return to normal.
“While the utility of hosting foreign military bases has always involved a calculus of risk versus the assumed assurance it provides, the perception among Gulf Arab states is certainly shifting,” Mohammad Ali Shabani, a Middle East analyst, told Al Jazeera. “The vulnerability of these assets is increasingly front-of-mind for host governments, who have not sought war, yet have been drawn into it without having had any real say.”
The US calculation
Washington faces a dilemma of its own. Bases in Europe or the Middle East give it the reach to fight faraway wars, but their presence has also provided Iran with a litany of targets.
In March, an Iranian drone hit a hangar at a British base in Cyprus that the US also uses for intelligence and logistics operations. Tehran threatened Bulgaria after reports emerged that the Eastern European NATO nation had allowed the US to use its Bezmer airbase for refuelling of planes used to attack Iran. Weeks later, Bulgaria’s defence minister announced that the US air tankers had left Bezmer for good, with the country’s president declaring that the “mission is over,” bringing relief to the village that the base draws its name from.
And in the Middle East, several key bases used by US troops have been almost rendered unusable, with those in Kuwait suffering the heaviest damage, say analysts. An attack on the Port of Shuaiba killed six US service members and destroyed an army operations centre. Iranian drones and missiles damaged aviation facilities and injured personnel at Ali Al Salem airbase, while strikes on Camp Buehring damaged maintenance and refuelling facilities.
In Qatar, an Iranian strike damaged the early warning radar system at Al Udeid airbase, which houses the headquarters of US Central Command’s (CENTCOM) air operations. In Bahrain, an Iranian drone struck communications equipment at the headquarters of the US Fifth Fleet.
This damage raises a question about how much the US can still use these bases once they come under attack. Gerd Nonneman, a professor of international relations and Gulf studies at Georgetown University in Qatar, told Al Jazeera the war had shown that some bases were “themselves very vulnerable” and “unable to fulfil many of the tasks they were established for”.
Why bases are harder to defend
Mark Hilborne, a senior lecturer at the Defence Studies Department at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera “large bases are indeed becoming more easily targeted”.
“One of the technologies that has allowed this, alongside fairly cheap ballistic missiles, is drones,” he added.
Iran has invested heavily in developing cheap, domestically produced drones that inflict disproportionate damage to targets and exhaust far more expensive interceptor missiles.
Meanwhile in the UK, drones present US airbases with different challenges. While the nature of the reported threat to RAF Mildenhall remains unclear, the Fairford case concerns an alleged plot. “The range of actors who might target bases has changed,” Urban Coningham, a research fellow and course lead at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) in the UK, told Al Jazeera. “Bases are more vulnerable, and that changes the risk calculation.
“Anyone can manufacture a drone in a basement … People looking to create mischief or mayhem can recruit organised criminals, making attacks harder to attribute.”
All of that, he said, makes bases “more vulnerable, and that changes the risk calculation”.
‘Policy conundrum’
As Washington moves some military assets out of bases in the Gulf and Europe, it could also come to rely more heavily on Israel, its closest ally in the Middle East. Shabani said there were “already signs that CENTCOM is moving towards using Israel as a key forward base”.
Israel launched the war on Iran in February alongside the US. With the oil and gas exports on which Gulf economies depend at risk, keeping US forces nearby allows Washington to respond, but it also leaves those forces exposed to Iranian attacks.
“The longer-term solution is to work with partners and ensure that allied forces are ready to fend for themselves,” RUSI’s Coningham said.
“There is a debate within the US policy establishment, and the Iranians are referencing it and saying that as long as US forces are there, they are a target,” he said. “That is the policy conundrum for the US. Ultimately, they can’t see any alternative to having bases in some form.”

https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120382.title: Lenbachhaus München | Maria Jarema: Freiheit in Zeiten der Extreme
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120382.author: Dorte Lena Eilers
https://www.nd-aktuell.de/artikel/120382.text:
- Kultur
- Lenbachhaus München
Maria Jarema: Freiheit in Zeiten der Extreme
Explosionen von Gefühlen: In einer Ausstellung im Münchner Lenbachhaus kann man Maria Jarema, die »Revolutionäre Kommissarin der Abstraktion«, entdecken.
Die Revolution trägt Pony. Folgt man der These einer großen überregionalen Tageszeitung, dass Frauen mit kurzem Vorderhaar derzeit sinnbildlich für das progressive, gar revolutionäre Lager stehen – Heidi Reichinnek, Elif Eralp, Kerstin Wolter –, würde die polnische Künstlerin Maria Jarema voll ins Bild passen. Mit wehendem Mantel, die bestiefelten Beine breitbeinig in den Boden gerammt, die Fransen des Ponys unter dem Schirm einer Arbeitermütze hervorlugend – so zeichnete sie der Theatermacher Tadeusz Kantor im Jahr 1990.
Modische Merkmale waren der 1908 im damaligen Österreich-Ungarn geborenen Künstlerin am Ende indes fremd. Was Maria Jarema heute so aufrüttelnd aktuell macht, ist ihre Kunst, die sich in Bildern, Skulpturen, Theaterkostümen um den Menschen und die Prämissen eines würdigen und freien Lebens sorgt. So führen uns im Münchner Lenbachhaus in der Ausstellung »Maria Jarema: Revolutionäre Kommissarin der Abstraktion« – benannt nach Kantors Skizzentitel – ihre Kunstwerke mit verspielter, verzerrter, deformierter Eindringlichkeit die Schrecken zivilisatorischer Verluste vor Augen. Verrohung, Krieg, Freiheitsentzug – Gefahren, die auch heute wieder drohen.
Grundvoraussetzung ihres vielfältigen Schaffens, das sich von der Malerei über Bildhauerei bis zum Theater erstreckte, war der Zustand der Freiheit. Die Freiheit von Zwang. Die Freiheit von Vorgaben, Moden, Schulen. Die Freiheit des Denkens. Aber auch eine Freiheit, die sich nicht in der narzisstischen Überheblichkeit eines Künstlergenies manifestierte, sondern stets mit der Welt und ihrem Leid verbunden blieb.
Wer ihre in ständiger Bewegung und also freier Entfaltung scheinenden Arbeiten betrachtet, fragt sich, warum diese Künstlerin, die den Kern künstlerischen Schaffens auch in ihren Reden benennen konnte, in Deutschland bislang so wenig bekannt ist. Auf der Konferenz der bildenden Künste im polnischen Nieborów erklärte Maria Jarema 1949 ganz schlicht: »Die Einschränkung der Freiheit der Künste ist Unsinn, denn sie zerstört sie.« Kunst unterliege vielmehr konstanter Veränderung: der Formen, Materialien, Techniken. Dieser Geist ist in der Münchner Ausstellung allzeit präsent.
Bereits im Eingangsbereich stoßen wir auf Schwarz-Weiß-Figuren, deren Fallen, Stürzen, Verschwinden vielfach gebrochen ist. Muskelpakete kopfloser Figurinen sind wie in Gunther von Hagens’ Körperwelten quasi enthäutet zu sehen. Ein Frauenkörper mit surrealistisch verzerrten Brüsten liegt am Boden. Menschenstudien voller Verletzlichkeit. Einen Schritt weiter blicken uns von Jarema gestaltete Handpuppen für Stücke des experimentellen Theaterprojekts Cricot entgegen, welches ihr Bruder Józef 1932 in Krakau ins Leben gerufen hatte. Zum Beispiel Joseph Goebbels mit eingeschlagener Nase.
Jarema war, nachdem sie 1929 an der Kunstakademie der berühmten Jagiellonen-Universität in Krakau angenommen worden war, früh politisch aktiv. 1932 gründete sie mit befreundeten Künstlerinnen und Künstlern die Grupa Krakowska (Krakauer Gruppe), um gegen die nationalkonservative Ausrichtung der Kunstakademie zu protestieren. Nach dem Krieg stellte sie sich der Doktrin des sozialistischen Realismus entgegen.
Den Krieg selbst erlebte sie in Form der deutschen Besatzung in Krakau, entging 1943 nur knapp einer Massenerschießung. Das Bild »Niemcy« (Deutsche) aus dem Jahr 1941 zeigt in augenfälliger Zweiteilung, durch einen blauen Strich markiert, das Eindringen des Krieges in den Alltag. Auf der linken Seite sind Menschen in stilvoll tapezierten Innenräumen zu erahnen, während sich auf der rechten Seite Soldaten nähern; das Gewehr des einen durchdringt bereits den blauen Trennstrich, die Grenze des Hauses.
Maria Jarema fand, immer in Resonanz zur europäischen modernen Kunst, die Freiheit in Zeiten der Extreme. 1956 entstand in Zusammenarbeit mit Tadeusz Kantor und Kazimierz Mikulski, einem dem Surrealismus nahestehenden Regisseur und Maler, ein weiteres Theaterprojekt, das Cricot 2.
Zwei Inszenierungen, »Der Tintenfisch« von Stanisław Witkiewicz sowie »Zirkus« von Mikulski, sind in Form auratischer Schwarz-Weiß-Filme in der Ausstellung zu sehen und zeigen, wie mit geringsten Mitteln – kleine Bühne, abgewetzter Vorhang, wenig Requisiten, dafür die exzentrischen Kostüme Maria Jaremas – ein Theater entstehen kann, das das Leben feiert. Warum die Projektionen lediglich in Kniehöhe angebracht sind, sodass sich jeder, der die Filmausschnitte in Gänze sehen will, dem Risiko eines Bandscheibenvorfalls ausgesetzt sieht, bleibt ein Rätsel des Ausstellungskonzepts.
In den Jahren vor ihrem frühen Tod – Jarema starb 1958 an Leukämie – begeisterte sie sich für kinetische Kunst, also bewegte Gemälde, die sie in Paris entdeckt hatte. Jarema versuchte den Effekt, der in den Pariser Werken in der Tat mechanisch hergestellt wurde, allein mit malerischen Mitteln umzusetzen. Insbesondere ihre Beschäftigung mit der Technik der Monotypie, einer Art Druckverfahren ohne Druckerpresse, erzeugte intensive, den Betrachter unmittelbar affizierende Werke. Ihre schwarz-weiß schraffierten »Figuren« aus dem Jahr 1953 scheinen wild miteinander zu ringen, wären sie nicht durch zwei rote Flächen innerlich miteinander verbunden. Ein Kampf oder eher doch eine liebevolle Umarmung?
Maria Jarema ist eine Entdeckung. Ihre Arbeit wirkt, wie sie selbst einmal über Kunst im Allgemeinen schrieb: »Wie Planeten, die an Wänden schlummern, explodieren Gemälde beim Kontakt mit den Inhalten der menschlichen Psyche – ein Ergebnis der Transformation, das wir, da uns dieses Phänomen fremd ist, vielleicht als ›chemisch‹ bezeichnen: Explosionen von Gefühlen.«
Maria Jarema: »Revolutionäre Kommissarin der Abstraktion«, Lenbachhaus, München, bis 25. April 2027.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
A Nova Maravilha Empreendimentos Imobiliários S.A. afirmou ter destinado aproximadamente 5 mil hectares de terras à reforma agrária ao longo de sua trajetória, mas os números foram contestados pela superintendência do Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária na Paraíba (Incra/PB).
A divergência surgiu após a empresa encaminhar uma nota de esclarecimento ao Brasil de Fato PB, em 10 de novembro de 2026, na qual também rejeitou qualquer associação ao ataque armado contra o Acampamento Marilene Dantas, localizado na área da antiga Usina Maravilha, entre Caaporã e Pedras de Fogo, no Litoral Sul da Paraíba.
Em entrevista à reportagem nesta quarta-feira (11), o superintendente do Incra na Paraíba, Antônio Barbosa, contestou o volume de terras mencionado pela empresa e apresentou informações sobre as negociações conduzidas nos últimos três anos, com a participação do Ministério Público Federal (MPF). Segundo ele, as propriedades formalmente ofertadas pela usina nessas tratativas somam aproximadamente 3 mil hectares, considerando áreas já destinadas e outras ainda em negociação.
A manifestação da empresa ocorre após a violência registrada na madrugada de domingo (8), quando, segundo relatos recebidos pelo Incra, homens armados efetuaram disparos e incendiaram 12 barracos no acampamento, onde vivem 42 famílias. O fogo também atingiu a vegetação da região. Conforme relatos dos moradores, mulheres, crianças e idosos precisaram buscar abrigo em uma área de mata.
O Movimento dos Trabalhadores Rurais Sem Terra (MST) cobra o aprofundamento das investigações para identificar não apenas os executores, mas também possíveis mandantes do ataque, além de medidas de proteção às famílias e uma solução para a disputa fundiária.
Empresa rejeita associação à violência
Na nota encaminhada à reportagem, assinada pelo Departamento Jurídico, a Nova Maravilha afirma que tomou conhecimento dos episódios de violência por meio da imprensa e que está buscando compreender as circunstâncias dos acontecimentos.
“A empresa repudia qualquer forma de violência, ameaça ou intimidação e ressalta que as alegações que pretendem associá-la a práticas dessa natureza são infundadas, não havendo qualquer elemento que autorize atribuir-lhe responsabilidade pelos acontecimentos noticiados”, declarou em nota, divulgada na íntegra no final da matéria.
O grupo afirmou ainda que sempre manteve uma relação pacífica e respeitosa com o MST e com os ocupantes de suas propriedades, privilegiando o diálogo e a solução institucional de eventuais divergências.
A companhia também destacou o que classificou como um histórico de contribuição para a reforma agrária. Em nota, afirmou ter destinado aproximadamente 5 mil hectares de terras a essa finalidade. Segundo a empresa, parte dos procedimentos de destinação já foi concluída, enquanto outros permanecem em análise pelo Incra. No entanto, não identificou os imóveis que compõem essa área, os municípios onde estão localizados nem o estágio de cada procedimento.
A manifestação também não apresenta uma proposta concreta para solucionar a situação das famílias do Acampamento Marilene Dantas.
Incra detalha negociações com a usina e contesta número divulgado
Em entrevista ao Brasil de Fato PB, Antônio Barbosa, contestou o total de 5 mil hectares anunciado pela empresa. Segundo ele, nas negociações acompanhadas pelo Instituto nos últimos três anos, a Usina Maravilha formalizou a oferta de três propriedades: o Engenho Dois Rios, que originou o Assentamento Vanderley Caixe, em Pedras de Fogo, com 1.936 hectares destinados à instalação de 323 famílias, e as fazendas Retirada e Tamanduá, que, juntas, não ultrapassam mil hectares.
“Passamos três anos em negociações duras e complexas junto ao Ministério Público Federal e à usina para viabilizar a oferta dessas três áreas: Dois Rios, Retirada e Tamanduá. A usina formalizou a oferta dessas terras; portanto, a informação veiculada na nota oficial da empresa mencionando 5.000 hectares é incorreta e sem lastro técnico”, afirmou Barbosa.
Fazendas Retirada e Tamanduá continuam em negociação
Barbosa detalhou o andamento das negociações das duas propriedades restantes. Nesta quarta-feira (11), a Fazenda Tamanduá foi qualificada, e a proposta do Incra será enviada à usina nas próximas horas. Já o laudo de avaliação da Fazenda Retirada será entregue até sexta-feira (13) para decisão da diretoria da Usina Maravilha.
O superintendente explicou que a empresa detém cerca de 3.200 hectares na Paraíba. Com os 1.936 hectares já destinados ao Assentamento Vanderley Caixe – criado em 25 de agosto de 2026 por decisão da 25ª Vara Federal de PE – somados às áreas em negociação, as tratativas já se aproximam de 3 mil hectares. A nota oficial do Incra acrescenta que outros 450 hectares da Tamanduá estão em processo de obtenção para as famílias do Acampamento Nova Esperança.
Possibilidade de cessão de parte da área do Marilene Dantas
Barbosa, também relatou uma possível mudança na posição da Usina Maravilha em relação à área ocupada pelas famílias do Acampamento Marilene Dantas, que existe desde 2013.
Segundo ele, durante os últimos três anos de negociações, a empresa resistiu a disponibilizar o imóvel para a reforma agrária. Recentemente, porém, Barbosa recebeu, por meio de um representante da usina, a informação de que a companhia estaria disposta a avaliar a oferta de uma parte da propriedade.
“Os assentados do Marilene Dantas ocupam a área desde 2013 e, até o momento, não abrem mão do imóvel. A usina mantinha-se irredutível em ceder o local, mas recebi há pouco a informação, por meio de um preposto da empresa, de que a Usina Maravilha está propensa a ofertar uma fração da área. Trata-se de um diálogo interno deles e a informação ainda não é oficial”, declarou.
Incra identifica propriedade com mais de 400 hectares em Pernambuco
Paralelamente às negociações com a Usina Maravilha, o Incra identificou uma propriedade com mais de 400 hectares no município de Itambé (PE), nas proximidades do Acampamento Marilene Dantas.
Segundo Antônio Barbosa, o imóvel é considerado uma alternativa viável para abrigar parte das famílias acampadas.
Como a propriedade está localizada majoritariamente em território pernambucano, o Incra/PB iniciou a instrução administrativa e encaminhou a documentação à superintendência do órgão em Pernambuco, responsável pela continuidade dos procedimentos.
Uma reunião entre as superintendências dos dois estados e outras entidades está prevista para 17 de novembro, com o objetivo de acelerar a tramitação necessária à eventual aquisição do imóvel.
MST cobra investigação dos mandantes e proteção às famílias
O MST permanece cobrando respostas sobre o ataque armado ocorrido em 8 de novembro no acampamento Marilene Dantas, quando homens incendiaram 12 barracos e atiraram contra o local. Para lideranças do movimento, a identificação de dois suspeitos pela Polícia Civil é apenas o primeiro passo, sendo necessária a apuração para alcançar os mandantes. O grupo reivindica proteção imediata para as famílias e a desapropriação da área por interesse social.
Reportagem encaminha novos questionamentos à empresa
Diante das divergências entre os números apresentados pela Nova Maravilha e as informações prestadas pelo superintendente, o Brasil de Fato PB encaminhou novos questionamentos à empresa.
A reportagem solicitou esclarecimentos sobre quais propriedades compõem os aproximadamente 5 mil hectares mencionados na nota oficial da usina, onde essas terras estão localizadas e quantos hectares tiveram, de fato, sua destinação à reforma agrária concluída. Além disso, o veículo questionou quais áreas da empresa permanecem sob análise do Incra.
Confira, a seguir, a íntegra da nota de esclarecimento da Nova Maravilha e da nota oficial do Incra/PB.
NOTA DE ESCLARECIMENTO – NOVA MARAVILHA
Recife, 10 de novembro de 2026.
Em atenção aos questionamentos encaminhados, a Nova Maravilha esclarece que tomou conhecimento dos supostos episódios de violência ocorridos no Acampamento Marilene Dantas por meio da imprensa e está buscando compreender as circunstâncias dos fatos relatados.
A empresa repudia qualquer forma de violência, ameaça ou intimidação e ressalta que as alegações que pretendem associá-la a práticas dessa natureza são infundadas, não havendo qualquer elemento que autorize atribuir-lhe responsabilidade pelos acontecimentos noticiados.
Cumpre destacar que a Nova Maravilha possui um histórico de contribuição efetiva para a reforma agrária, tendo destinado aproximadamente 5 mil hectares de terras a essa finalidade, parte dos quais já teve seu processo de destinação concluído, enquanto outras áreas permanecem em análise pelo Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária (INCRA). Essa atuação evidencia sua disposição histórica de colaborar com as políticas públicas de acesso à terra e com a solução institucional das questões fundiárias.
Ao longo de sua trajetória, a empresa sempre manteve uma relação pacífica e respeitosa com o Movimento dos Trabalhadores Rurais Sem Terra (MST) e com os ocupantes de suas propriedades, privilegiando o diálogo e a solução institucional de eventuais divergências.
Nesse contexto, a Nova Maravilha considera absolutamente incompatível com sua história e sua conduta a tentativa de vinculá-la a episódios de violência, sobretudo quando não existem elementos concretos que sustentem semelhante imputação.
Por fim, a empresa reafirma seu compromisso com a legalidade, a paz no campo e o respeito à dignidade das pessoas envolvidas, permanecendo à disposição das autoridades competentes para contribuir com o esclarecimento dos fatos.
Nova Maravilhas Empreendimentos Imobiliários S.A.
Departamento Jurídico.
NOTA OFICIAL – INCRA/PB
O Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária na Paraíba (INCRA/PB) manifesta profunda indignação e repúdio à violência registrada na madrugada deste domingo (8), no Acampamento Marilene Dantas, localizado na área da antiga Usina Maravilha, entre os municípios de Caaporã e Pedras de Fogo, no Litoral Sul da Paraíba, onde vivem 42 famílias. Segundo os relatos recebidos, homens armados efetuaram disparos e incendiaram nove barracos, colocando em risco a vida de trabalhadores rurais, mulheres e crianças. O fogo também atingiu a vegetação da região.
A violência no campo é inaceitável. Nenhuma disputa pela posse ou propriedade da terra pode justificar ameaças, intimidações ou atentados contra a vida e a integridade das pessoas. O INCRA espera das autoridades competentes a rigorosa apuração dos fatos, a identificação e responsabilização dos envolvidos, observados os procedimentos legais, e a adoção de medidas que assegurem a proteção das famílias.
Diante de manifestações públicas que atribuem ao INCRA falta de celeridade e responsabilidade na busca de uma solução para a situação fundiária, o Instituto considera necessário esclarecer os fatos. É injusto atribuir à autarquia omissão diante de uma realidade que envolve procedimentos legais complexos, decisões judiciais, direitos de terceiros e a atuação de diferentes instituições públicas. A gravidade dos acontecimentos exige responsabilidade, cooperação e compromisso com soluções efetivas, e não a transferência de responsabilidades entre órgãos públicos.
A atuação do INCRA na região demonstra que a instituição vem adotando medidas concretas para ampliar o acesso à terra. Parte do imóvel rural Engenho Dois Rios foi obtida por meio de decisão da 25ª Vara da Justiça Federal de Pernambuco. Na área, o Instituto criou, em 25 de agosto de 2026, o Projeto de Assentamento Vanderley Caixe, em Pedras de Fogo, com aproximadamente 1.936 hectares e capacidade prevista para 323 famílias. Outros 450 hectares da Gleba Tamanduá, pertencente ao mesmo imóvel, encontram-se em processo de obtenção, com perspectiva de destinação às famílias do Acampamento Nova Esperança.
Em relação ao Acampamento Marilene Dantas, a empresa Usina Maravilhas S.A., proprietária da área, comunicou ao INCRA e à Comissão de Soluções Fundiárias do Tribunal de Justiça da Paraíba (TJPB) que não pretende disponibilizar o imóvel para o Programa Nacional de Reforma Agrária (PNRA). Atualmente, não existe processo administrativo de obtenção dessa área pelo Instituto. Isso, entretanto, não significa ausência de atuação institucional. O INCRA participa, em articulação com a Comissão de Soluções Fundiárias, da busca por alternativas fundiárias que possam viabilizar o atendimento às famílias, respeitando as competências de cada instituição e os procedimentos previstos em lei.
O INCRA não se exime de suas responsabilidades, mas tampouco pode assumir atribuições que não lhe competem ou desconsiderar exigências legais para a obtenção de imóveis rurais. A construção de uma solução duradoura exige diálogo, segurança jurídica, cooperação entre os poderes públicos e, sobretudo, compromisso com a vida e a dignidade das famílias.
O Instituto considera que o momento exige a união de esforços das instituições responsáveis pela mediação do conflito, pela segurança pública e pela execução das políticas de acesso à terra. Divergências sobre os caminhos e os prazos de atuação não podem se sobrepor à necessidade urgente de proteger as pessoas e construir soluções.
O INCRA/PB manifesta solidariedade às famílias do Acampamento Marilene Dantas, especialmente àquelas que perderam suas moradias, e reafirma seu compromisso com a reforma agrária, a defesa dos direitos humanos, a legalidade e a busca de soluções pacíficas para os conflitos fundiários.
A violência não pode ser naturalizada. A responsabilidade pública exige mais do que declarações: exige diálogo, cooperação institucional e ações concretas para que nenhuma família tenha sua vida ameaçada em razão da luta pelo acesso à terra.
Instituto Nacional de Colonização e Reforma Agrária – INCRA/PB

https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/saudi.title: Is Saudi Arabia expanding its ballistic missile programme?
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/saudi.author: Paul Iddon
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/saudi.text:
Is Saudi Arabia expanding its ballistic missile programme?
Saudi Arabia is believed to be expanding its Chinese-designed ballistic missile arsenal as it faces an unprecedented barrage of missile and drone attacks from Yemen's Houthi forces.
Satellite imagery analysed by American researchers suggests the kingdom is expanding its ballistic missile plant at al-Duwadimi in Riyadh Province to build larger solid-fuel missiles capable of carrying heavier payloads across greater distances.
Fighting between the kingdom and the Iran-aligned Yemeni group has intensified since July, shattering a UN-brokered truce that had largely held since 2022.
The Houthis have stepped up missile and drone attacks on Saudi cities, airports and energy infrastructure, retaliating for what they call a Saudi "blockade" of ports and airports in Houthi-controlled areas of Yemen.
Analysts have told Middle East Eye that the renewed confrontation with the Houthis has given the kingdom's arsenal added significance.
