Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Riyadh is reported to have begun building ballistic missiles domestically with Chinese assistance in 2021, but its relationship with Beijing over the weapons dates back several decades.
In the 1980s, shortly after establishing the Royal Saudi Strategic Missile Force (RSSMF), Riyadh turned to Beijing for its first ballistic missiles.
Beijing supplied conventional DF-3 intermediate-range ballistic missiles with an impressive range of over 2,000 miles but incredibly low accuracy.
Saudi Arabia reportedly acquired more accurate DF-21 medium-range ballistic missiles with conventional payloads in 2007.
In September, footage of missile debris in Yemen indicated that Saudi Arabia had fired a DF-15A short-range ballistic missile, potentially marking its first combat use of one of its Chinese-designed missiles.
Ameneh Mehvar, Middle East senior analyst at the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (Acled) project, said the expansion reflected a broader Saudi strategy of diversifying its military capabilities.
"Riyadh continues to invest heavily in advanced US-supplied aircraft and defence systems, while Chinese-designed ballistic missiles provide an additional means of conducting long-range strikes without exposing aircraft to enemy air defences," Mehvar told MEE.
"Expanding domestic missile production could also give Saudi Arabia greater control over its strike capabilities and reduce its dependence on foreign deliveries," she said.
'Less exposed to geopolitical shifts'
Sim Tack, vice-president of technology and intelligence solutions at AllSource Analysis, says the satellite imagery provides a strong indication that the programme is continuing to advance.
"The expansion of infrastructure to support ballistic missile developments is notable in the sense that it confirms continued efforts to expand indigenous missile design and production capabilities," Tack told MEE.
'Domestic production capabilities and their continued development indicate most of all that Saudi Arabia intends to be self-sufficient in the production of ballistic missiles'
- Sim Tack, AllSource Analysis
"Given the regional dynamics, this intent fits with the ambitions to balance missile capabilities against Iran and its allies such as the Houthis," he said.
The expansion also points to Riyadh's ambition to source more of its missiles domestically.
Its traditional reliance on western suppliers for military equipment has left it with limited options in the ballistic missile sector, partly because those countries have sought to avoid fuelling regional proliferation of surface-to-surface missiles and related technology.
That has helped push Saudi Arabia towards China as a discreet supplier of the weapons.
"Domestic production capabilities and their continued development indicate most of all that Saudi Arabia intends to be self-sufficient in the production of ballistic missiles," Tack said.
"Domestic production, and possibly even indigenous design, of ballistic missiles would allow Saudi Arabia to be less exposed to geopolitical shifts that could limit access to the weapon systems they would need to maintain a viable deterrent or even offensive capability," he added.
Recent developments related to US military support to Ukraine, the rapid depletion of American weapon stockpiles, and sensitivities around sourcing military equipment from China underline the increased importance of having such a localised production capability.
Deterrence and nuclear ambitions
Sebastien Roblin, a widely published military aviation journalist, argues that the purpose of the missile force should be understood in two ways: its ability to deter regional adversaries and its potential contribution to actual military operations.
"Most importantly, the missile force gives Saudi Arabia a way to practically deliver a nuclear strike, should Riyadh ever develop or otherwise acquire nuclear warheads – something looking distinctly possible today, particularly as Riyadh builds up its alliance with Pakistan," Roblin told MEE.
"While Pakistan and Israel have independently modified US fighters for nuclear delivery, indigenously built ballistic missiles are arguably a more practical debut delivery platform, especially as Iran currently has limited ballistic missile defence capability," he said.
"Importantly, for strategic nuclear deterrence, such missiles don't have to be particularly accurate."
Solid-fuel missiles, like those Saudi Arabia is reportedly developing, offer another important advantage: they can be stored ready for launch indefinitely, unlike liquid-fuelled missiles, which require more preparation.
Keeping solid-fuel ballistic missiles on standby also reduces the likelihood that an adversary could destroy the kingdom's deterrent capability before it has a chance to launch.
"In theory, the ballistic missile force also exerts conventional deterrence," Roblin said.
"Though in the current context of the attacks that have already rained down on cities across the Middle East in the last few years, I'm not sure Saudi conventional ballistic missiles can scare Tehran or the Houthis after what they've already endured recently."
The challenge of precision
If Riyadh intends to use its conventionally armed ballistic missiles to achieve specific military objectives, rather than simply inflict what Roblin describes as "unpredictable destruction and psychological shock", accuracy will be critical.
The DF-15A and DF-21 missiles are considerably more accurate than the older DF-3As. They can reportedly strike within 30 to 45 metres of their intended targets, less than half the length of a football field, whereas the older DF-3As could miss by several football field lengths.
But striking hardened targets, such as enemy missile silos, would require considerably greater precision to ensure a direct hit.
"China has achieved higher precision via satellite guidance in its later DF-15 and DF-21 series missiles, so perhaps it has or may eventually pass that technology along," Roblin said.
"Alternatively, tactical nuclear warheads can also be employed to reduce the precision needed."
Drawing on US-Israeli strikes against the Houthis and Iran since 2025, as well as four years of Russian missile attacks on Ukraine, Roblin cautions against overstating what Saudi Arabia's ballistic missile arsenal could achieve in a major conflict.
In the US-Israeli campaign against Iran, he noted, the most prominent and vulnerable targets have already been attacked. Hitting hardened underground facilities and mobile missile launchers requires persistent aerial drone surveillance and extremely rapid targeting and strike capabilities.
Concealed facilities in Iran also require sophisticated intelligence operations to identify and locate them before they can be attacked.
"Despite its comparative shortcomings, the RSSMF helps Riyadh develop a strike capability for future conflicts in which US support might be lacking; and thus might mitigate the asymmetry with Tehran's massive investment in strategic strike weapons," Roblin said.
"Remove the US from the picture, and suddenly the RSSMF might be called upon to do more heavy lifting against vulnerable static targets in future conflicts."
From deterrence to combat
Mehvar says the reported use of a Saudi DF-15A in Yemen in September, if confirmed, could signal that the kingdom's ballistic missiles are taking on a more active combat role rather than serving primarily as a deterrent.
"Overall, Riyadh appears to be broadening its military options while maintaining its longstanding reliance on US military technology and security cooperation," she said.
Tack, however, cautions that Saudi Arabia's limited history of operational ballistic missile use makes it difficult to determine how the kingdom intends to deploy the weapons.
'Riyadh appears to be broadening its military options while maintaining its longstanding reliance on US military technology and security cooperation'
- Ameneh Mehvar, Acled
"Ballistic missiles do offer methods for deep strike capabilities that Saudi Arabia has struggled to establish using their air force," he said. "Throughout Saudi operations in Yemen over the past decade, the limited effectiveness of Saudi air strikes has always stood out."
The limited accuracy and vulnerability of Saudi aircraft in contested airspace have also constrained the effectiveness of its air force. Ballistic missiles could help Riyadh overcome some of those limitations.
But doing so would require an effective intelligence capability to identify targets and guide strikes – an area in which Saudi Arabia has struggled without extensive external support.
"So while there may be an intent to apply a ballistic missile arsenal in a tactical manner on the battlefield, there are many other hurdles for Saudi Arabia to overcome to do so effectively," Tack said.
"The role of ballistic missiles as a general deterrent, and in a deep-strike role against strategic targets, appears much more viable."
A substantial missile arsenal, backed by large stockpiles, could eventually give Saudi Arabia the ability to strike Iran independently, potentially changing the balance of power between the two countries.
"Up until today, Saudi Arabia and several other countries in the region have been wholly dependent on US operations to provide a viable option to strike back at Iran," Tack said.
"Having their own viable strike options would at the very least reduce the reliance on the US in shaping negotiations with, and military action against Iran."
Sending a message
Roblin sees the reported September DF-15A launch as potentially serving two purposes: testing the weapon operationally and sending a political message to both the Houthis and Iran that Saudi Arabia has the capacity to escalate militarily.
He believes the RSSMF could carry out further combat tests to calibrate its capabilities and signal its willingness to use them.
"However, if Saudi Arabia is producing missiles at large enough scale - and has upgraded them to the requisite degree of accuracy for tactical effectiveness - it could choose to employ them more regularly much like the US has employed ATACMS and PrSM ballistic missiles," Roblin said.
"The capability can be a useful addition to the toolkit, though over Yemen specifically Saudi fighters arguably have enough free rein that it's not particularly urgent (despite the occasional aircraft loss)."
Saudi fighter jets can also penetrate Iranian airspace, but doing so involves greater operational risks, including evading air defences and conducting mid-air refuelling to sustain long-range missions. Ballistic missiles could offer a less complicated means of carrying out deep strikes.
Nevertheless, Roblin does not expect the missile force to replace the Royal Saudi Air Force (RSAF) as the kingdom's primary striking force unless Riyadh experiences a more prolonged breakdown in relations with Washington.
"Aviation represents a more sustainable and flexible combat capability, which is why the countries you see investing more in missiles over aviation tend to be those like Iran which rightly anticipate that their manned warplanes are likely to be mostly neutralised by enemy air power," he said.
"That's not the case for the RSAF, though it certainly may benefit from working in tandem with the kingdom's surface-to-surface strike capability."

https://www.humanite.fr/monde/donald-tru.title: Premier sénateur noir de l’État depuis 146 ans, soutenu par Bernie Sanders… Qui est Scott Colom, élu dans le Mississippi ?
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/donald-tru.author: Benjamin König
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/donald-tru.text:
Le symbole est fort dans cet État historiquement esclavagiste et ségrégationniste, où le dernier sénateur noir élu en 1875 était né esclave. Mais Scott Colom a d’abord axé sa campagne sur des thèmes sociaux, l’accès aux soins et l’aide alimentaire, dans un des États les plus pauvres du pays.
Il aura fallu une semaine de dépouillement pour que sa victoire soit annoncée : Scott Colom, un procureur de l’État âgé de 43 ans, a été élu sénateur pour le parti démocrate lors du scrutin des midterms du 3 novembre. Il a battu la sénatrice républicaine sortante, Cindy Hyde-Smith, et devient ainsi le premier sénateur noir du Mississippi depuis… cent quarante-six ans. Le dernier en date, Blanche Bruce, était né esclave et avait été élu en 1875, avant d’être remplacé par un ancien soldat confédéré raciste, exécuteur de politiques ségrégationnistes.
Le Mississippi est un État du sud traditionnellement républicain, profondément marqué par les divisions raciales et la ségrégation à l’encontre des Noirs. En 2024, Donald Trump avait remporté l’État avec près de 23 points d’avance, ce qui donne une idée de l’exploit réalisé par Scott Colom. Ce dernier a notamment axé sa campagne sur l’accès aux soins pour tous les citoyens et l’aide alimentaire, que sa prédécesseure avait coupé, dans l’un des États les plus pauvres du pays.
Soutenu par Bernie Sanders
Considéré comme un progressiste aux États-Unis, le sénateur appartient à l’aile gauche du parti démocrate, et avait été soutenu par Bernie Sanders. Celui-ci l’a félicité « pour sa victoire à l’élection et pour avoir fait l’histoire en tant que premier sénateur noir du Mississippi », saluant « son programme audacieux s’attaquant aux géants de la tech, à la classe des milliardaires et à la corruption à Washington ».
Ce résultat est aussi une petite revanche de l’histoire : voici trois ans, sa nomination au sein du système judiciaire fédéral avait été bloquée par Cindy Hyde-Smith. C’est désormais lui qui nommera les juges dans le Mississippi.
Être le journal de la paix, notre défi quotidien
Depuis Jaurès, la défense de la paix est dans notre ADN.
- Qui informe encore aujourd’hui sur les actions des pacifistes pour le désarmement ?
- Combien de médias rappellent que les combats de décolonisation ont encore cours, et qu’ils doivent être soutenus ?
- Combien valorisent les solidarités internationales, et s’engagent sans ambiguïté aux côtés des exilés ?
Nos valeurs n’ont pas de frontières.
Aidez-nous à soutenir le droit à l’autodétermination et l’option de la paix.
Je veux en savoir plus !

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: US envoys arrive in Moscow for Russia-Ukraine talks with Putin
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
US envoys arrive in Moscow for Russia-Ukraine talks with Putin
The meeting with Kushner and Witkoff comes after two days of trilateral talks in the UAE yielded no breakthrough.
United States envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have arrived in Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in their latest push for a peace deal in Ukraine.
Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s special envoy, met Kushner and Witkoff at their plane on Thursday morning and accompanied them to central Moscow.
The meeting comes on the heels of two days of trilateral peace talks in the United Arab Emirates that concluded in the capital, Abu Dhabi, on Wednesday with news of another planned major prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on ending the nearly five-year war.
The US said differences remained on major issues, including territory, but some progress had been made on post-war security guarantees.
Kyiv has strongly rejected Putin’s demands to surrender all of its eastern region of Donbas in return for peace.
The Abu Dhabi talks were the first direct negotiations between Russia and Ukraine mediated by the US in nine months.
Al Jazeera’s Yulia Shapovalova, reporting from Moscow, said one of the goals of Thursday’s visit would be for the US team to persuade Putin to invite Europeans to the negotiation process.
“Ukraine and the US want the European partners to be involved while Moscow is adamant about talks without the Europeans, and that’s why they’ve been largely excluded from the process,” she said.
Shapovalova added that the US delegation would bring Putin an updated proposal for a peace plan and the presence of Dmitriev in the talks was an indication that they would address some of the more complex issues.
European leaders meet in Dublin
During the US-backed effort to revive talks, leaders from more than 40 European countries gathered in Dublin on Thursday for a summit focused on the continent’s security.
The meeting of the European Political Community (EPC) brought together heads of state and government from the European Union and other European countries, including the United Kingdom. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte also attended.
The EPC was established in 2022 as a forum for countries both inside and outside the 27-nation EU.
Zelenskyy and his European allies are expected to discuss this week’s talks in Abu Dhabi.
Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, and Witkoff are scheduled to meet Zelenskyy in Dublin on Friday after talking to Putin.
Audrey Macalpine, reporting from Kyiv, said Ukrainians do not believe the talks in Moscow will yield results. “Over the past two days, we saw just another prisoner exchange, which has been the case in previous talks,” the correspondent said.
“When it comes to the negotiations, not much has changed in terms of where these two sides stand,” Macalpine added. “Perhaps the biggest thing of note [in the talks] was that they took place at all.”
Meanwhile, French Minister Delegate for European Affairs Benjamin Haddad on Thursday said the EU will approve more sanctions against Russia.
“On Monday, we will take new sanctions against Russia on 150 additional entities, 50 banks, and it’s France which proposed the bulk of the entities to add,” Haddad told LCI television.
Russia strikes Ukrainian capital, energy facilities
As talks continue, Russia launched ballistic missiles and dozens of combat drones at Ukraine overnight, killing one person, Ukrainian officials said on Thursday.
A woman was killed and five people injured when a drone hit a residential block in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko wrote on Telegram. Out of the 123 Russian combat drones used, 89 were shot down, the military said.
Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov said Russian strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure overnight caused power outages in nine Ukrainian regions, namely Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa, Rivne, Sumy, Kharkiv and Cherkasy.
Separately, Ukraine’s military said it had struck Russia’s five largest oil refineries since October 30, including those in Omsk, Kirishi, Ryazan, Nizhny Novgorod and Yaroslavl. In a post on Telegram, the General Staff said the smaller Novokuibyshevsk and Saratov refineries had also been hit.
Meanwhile, Russia’s Investigative Committee said a Russian military serviceman was killed after the car he was driving was blown up in the Pushkinsky District of St Petersburg on Thursday.
Moscow has blamed Ukraine for previous assassinations of senior military officials and people linked to its war effort. There was no immediate comment from Ukraine about the latest incident.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Morre embaixador da Rússia nos EUA aos 66 anos
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Serguei Monin
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O embaixador da Rússia nos Estados Unidos, Alexander Darchiev, morreu nesta quarta-feira (11), aos 66 anos. A informação foi confirmada pelo Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia.
“Um diplomata excepcional, líder experiente, bom amigo e mentor faleceu. Um profissional de excelência e um brilhante especialista em assuntos ligados às Américas, Alexander Nikitich Darchiev atuou em uma das áreas mais importantes da política externa russa“, declarou o Ministério, que emitiu um comunicado lamentando com “profundo pesar o falecimento repentino” do diplomata russo.
“Alexander Nikitich dedicou toda a sua vida à firme defesa dos interesses da Rússia na América do Norte e à construção de relações de igualdade com os Estados Unidos”, diz a nota.
Posteriormente, a porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia, Maria Zakharova, afirmou que o embaixador faleceu em decorrência de uma doença crônica.
“Alexander Nikitich faleceu hoje em Moscou em decorrência de uma doença crônica. Forneceremos mais informações sobre a data e o local do funeral”, afirmou ela em um comunicado em seu canal no Telegram.
A porta-voz da chancelaria russa afirmou que o país está recebendo inúmeras condolências de todo o mundo em relação ao ocorrido.
O porta-voz do secretário-geral da ONU, Farhan Haqm, declarou que as Nações Unidas expressaram condolências à Rússia pelo falecimento de seu embaixador nos Estados Unidos. “Expressamos nossas condolências à sua família e ao governo russo”, disse, em entrevista à RIA Novosti.
Quem é Darchiev
Em 6 de março de 2025, o presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, nomeou Alexander Darchiev, então Diretor do Departamento do Atlântico Norte do Ministério das Relações Exteriores da Rússia, como Embaixador Extraordinário e Plenipotenciário da Federação Russa nos Estados Unidos.
Darchiev nasceu em 14 de maio de 1960. Em outubro de 2014, foi nomeado Embaixador da Rússia no Canadá, cargo que ocupou até janeiro de 2021, quando retornou à sua posição como Diretor do Departamento da América do Norte (renomeado Departamento do Atlântico Norte em janeiro de 2025). Em 2016, recebeu o título de Embaixador Extraordinário e Plenipotenciário.
Alexander Darchiev assumiu a Embaixada em Washington em março de 2025. Ao mesmo tempo, tornou-se observador permanente da Rússia junto à Organização dos Estados Americanos.

Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills surgeon, child and patients
An Israeli air strike hit Nasser Medical Complex in the Gaza Strip early on Thursday, killing at least six Palestinians, including a surgeon, a child and patients, and wounding 20 others.
The strike hit the hospital's surgical buildings at around 1 am local time. The partially functioning complex in Khan Younis remains the last major referral hospital operating in southern Gaza, despite being under extreme strain.
Dr Rizq Abu Shaira, 53, was among those killed, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The surgeon was treating patients when the strike hit, local media reported.
At least one child and a disabled patient were also killed. Other patients and medical staff, including women and children, were wounded.
The ministry condemned the attack, describing it as a flagrant violation of international law.

“The continued targeting of hospitals and their medical facilities exacerbates the suffering of the sick and wounded, and threatens what remains of the ability of the health sector to provide its services,” it said.
Two missiles struck the building's roof, penetrating the third floor before exploding on the second, The New York Times reported.
A hospital official said the strike caused extensive damage to the intensive care and surgical wards, including both the male and female departments.
The hospital's surgical ward has since been forced to suspend operations.
Hamas held the so-called Board of Peace responsible for the attack, saying it reflected Israel's continued impunity amid international silence and the failure to stop its violations.
The Israeli military confirmed the strikes, saying it had targeted “a senior terrorist and additional Hamas terrorists as they were hiding at the Nasser Hospital”.
Ynet reported that the attack targeted Khaled Abu Anza, whom it described as the commander of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade.
Middle East Eye could not independently verify the reports.
The Israeli military has claimed in recent months that Hamas was using Nasser Hospital for military purposes.
Similar claims have been made by the army since the start of Israel's genocide in Gaza in 2023, often preceding attacks on hospitals. The Palestinian movement has repeatedly denied them.
“The Israeli occupation's claims that Nasser Medical Complex was being used for military purposes are repeated lies intended to provide cover for the systematic targeting of the healthcare sector,” Hamas said on Thursday.
Attacks on hospitals
The World Health Organization (WHO) says 94 percent of hospitals in Gaza have been fully or partially destroyed during Israel's genocide.
Israeli forces have also killed and abducted hundreds of doctors, nurses and other medical workers.
Nasser Hospital, the second-largest medical complex in the Gaza Strip before the war, has been targeted at least seven times since October 2023.
In August 2025, an Israeli double-tap attack on the hospital killed 20 people, including Palestinian journalists, medical staff and first responders.
Among those killed were Middle East Eye contributors Mohamed Salama and Ahmed Abu Aziz.
International law experts have said the attack may have amounted to war crimes.

https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.title: College students rally in support of Starbucks baristas urging boycott over contract impasse
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.author: Michael Sainato
https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text:
Starbucks baristas, students, elected officials and allies are holding rallies at over 40 college campuses across the US on Thursday to support the Starbucks Workers United boycott campaign as the union nears five years of deadlock with the company over contract negotiations.
Starbucks Workers United is seeking better pay and stronger staffing levels, including a $17 an hour minimum wage for baristas and a minimum staffing of three workers per store. It has called on the public to boycott Starbucks until its first contract is reached.
More than 700 Starbucks stores have voted to unionize, representing more than 12,000 baristas. It typically takes over 450 days for a new labor union to negotiate and reach its first contract, but it has been nearly five years since the first Starbucks store in Buffalo, New York, voted to unionize in December 2021.
Starbucks Workers United began to focus on college campuses in 2023, calling on campuses to cancel their contracts with Starbucks in protest against the company’s response to union-organizing efforts. In response, Cornell University and Pomona College did not renew their contracts with the company, while UCLA stopped offering Starbucks products in their cafes.
Rallies and events will take place at private and public universities across the country, including the University of Pennsylvania, Northwestern and the University of Washington.
The union push come ahead of the company’s busy holiday season, including Starbucks’ Red Cup Day on 17 November, when customers receive a reusable holiday cup.
“Starbucks has been fueling the working class for decades, but they’re failing the workers that fuel their profits,” said Andrew Trinklein, a barista who is participating in an event at the University of Texas at Austin. “We’re really trying to push and get support from college campus students… in joining the boycott.”
His store recently unionized, and he expressed shock at how the company hired pricey union avoidance consultants in attempts to deter workers from unionizing. Starbucks has reportedly spent tens of millions of dollars related to union avoidance, though it has not disclosed the full costs relating to its union-organizing efforts.
Trinklein emphasized that employees are currently employed at-will, meaning they have no just-cause job security protections.
“Right now it’s just a toss-up whether we have a job tomorrow or not. Say they don’t like something that we’re doing – say we don’t write on a cup. We could be fired for it tomorrow,” Trinklein said, referring to the company’s policy requiring employees to write friendly messages on cups for customers. “But with this contract, that won’t be possible. We’ll have protections from stuff like that.”
Efforts to pressure Starbucks to negotiate were temporarily paused when the union and Starbucks reached an agreement on a path forward in February 2024. But negotiations broke down shortly after Brian Niccol took over as Starbucks CEO.
Niccol previously served as CEO of Chipotle from 2018 to 2024, and under his tenure, the company agreed to pay $240,000 to former workers as part of a settlement over a store closing in Maine after it unionized, which the National Labor Relations Board said was illegal. Chipotle has denied wrongdoing.
In recent years, Starbucks has been found guilty of violating federal labor law by the NLRB in several cases regarding its responses to union-organizing efforts.
In a statement, a Starbucks spokesperson said: “Workers United represents approximately 5% of our US partners, and we believe actions like these divert attention from the work at the bargaining table.”
“Our partners and coffeehouses are focused on bringing the joy of the holidays to life for our customers. Based on our experience with prior similar actions, we don’t expect any meaningful disruption and look forward to serving our customers through the holidays,” a spokesperson for Starbucks wrote in an email.
The spokesperson noted that “according to independent research, Starbucks offers the best overall pay and benefits in the industry, worth on average more than $30 per hour and including comprehensive healthcare, 100% upfront tuition coverage, company stock and up to 18 weeks of paid parental leave for partners working as little as 20 hours a week, which is why our turnover is among the industry’s lowest, and nearly 3 million people applied to wear the green apron last year”.

https://www.humanite.fr/en-debat/cop31/l.text:
Gérard Le Puill
Du 9 au 20 novembre, la COP 31 sur le climat se déroule à Antalya en Turquie. Onze ans plus tôt, la Cop 21 de Paris avait retenu le chiffre de + 2°C, voire +1,5°C si possible, à ne pas dépasser en 2100 en moyenne mondiale par rapport aux températures du début du XIXème siècle. Mais ce dernier chiffre est déjà en voie de dépassement dans les pays européens. Ajoutons que cette année 2026 est très révélatrice de la multitude des dégâts que provoque le réchauffement climatique en cours. En France comme dans beaucoup d’autres pays, la sécheresse et les incendies ont détruit des récoltes et des forêts tout en faisant croître les émissions de CO2. Des orages de grêle et des inondations ont également causé de gros dégâts, dont les réparations sont coûteuses et émettrices de gaz à effet de serre....

https://taz.de/US-Kongresswahlen/!622941.title: US-Kongresswahlen: Schwarzer Demokrat gewinnt Senatssitz in Mississippi
https://taz.de/US-Kongresswahlen/!622941.author: Hansjürgen Mai
https://taz.de/US-Kongresswahlen/!622941.text:
US-Kongresswahlen: Schwarzer Demokrat gewinnt Senatssitz in Mississippi
Scott Colom wird der erste afroamerikanische Senator aus dem erzkonservativen Bundesstaat seit 1881. Der äußerts knappe Ausgang war gespannt erwartet worden.
Die Demokraten haben ihre neu erlangte Mehrheit im US-Senat weiter ausgebaut. Wie mehrere US-Medien am Mittwochabend bestätigten, hat der Demokrat Scott Colom neusten Auszählungen zufolge die Senatswahl in Mississippi für sich entschieden. Der US-Bundesstaat ist damit, vor Alaska, der Vorletzte, in dem nun ein Sieger feststeht. Colom ist der erste schwarze Senator seit 1881, der Mississippi in Washington vertreten wird.
Er ist auch der erste Demokrat seit 44 Jahren, der in Mississippi eine Senatswahl gewinnen konnte. Demokraten haben in den Zwischenwahlen, die in der vergangenen Woche abgehalten wurden, damit insgesamt acht Senatssitze dazugewonnen. Der Sieg eines Demokraten in dem ultrakonservativen Südstaat dürfte jedoch die größte Überraschung dabei sein. Selbst der Sieg in Texas kann da nicht mithalten.
Der 43-jährige Colom arbeitet als Staatsanwalt und fokussierte sich im Wahlkampf auf Bezahlbarkeit. Er konnte damit vor allem die schwarze Wählerschaft in Mississippi überzeugen. Wie im Rest des Landes trug auch in Mississippi die allgemeine Unzufriedenheit mit der Regierung von US-Präsident Donald Trump und die schwierige wirtschaftliche Lage zu seinem Sieg bei.
Die demokratische Parteispitze feierte den Erfolg des neu gewählten Senators und erklärte, die diesjährigen Wahlergebnisse hätten bewiesen, dass die amerikanischen Südstaaten sich zunehmend zu einem umkämpften politischen Schauplatz entwickeln.
„Scott Colom ist die einzige Person, die das hätte erreichen können. Ich wusste es in dem Moment, als ich ihn zum ersten Mal traf. Gemeinsam mit seinem Team und seinen freiwilligen Helfern hat Scott einen herausragenden Wahlkampf geführt und neu definiert, was für Demokraten im Süden möglich ist“, sagte der demokratische Senatsfraktionschef Chuck Schumer auf X.
Schwarze Demokraten, darunter der Abgeordnete Bennie Thomas (Mississippi), die Senatorin Angela Alsobrooks (Maryland) und der Senator Raphael Warnock (Florida), unterstützten Coloms Kandidatur von Anfang an. Auch Schumer trug zu seinem Erfolg bei. Er rekrutierte Colom; half ihm Gelder zu sammeln; und stelle ihm Ressourcen zur Verfügung.
Schwarze Wähler ausschlaggebend
Auch wenn es am Ende ein denkbar knapper Sieg sein wird – aktuell liegen zwischen Colom und seiner republikanischen Kontrahentin, der amtierende Senatorin Cindy Hyde‑Smith, nur etwas mehr als 4.600 Stimmen und 0,5 Prozentpunkte –, gab es bereits in den vergangenen Jahren Anzeichen dafür, dass Mississippi als erster Bundesstaat im „tiefen Süden“ der USA einen Demokraten wählen könnte.
Mississippi hat den landesweit höchsten Anteil an schwarzen Wählern und seit Jahren sind die Wahlergebnisse dort deutlich knapper als in den benachbarten Südstaaten. Die bisherige Auswertung der Ergebnisse zeigte eine hohe Wahlbeteiligung im Mississippi-Delta. In dieser Region stellen schwarze Wähler in vielen Bezirken die Mehrheit.
Insgesamt verschob sich das politische Spektrum in fast allen Teilen des Bundesstaates nach links – im Vergleich zur Präsidentschaftswahl 2024, in der Trump Mississippi noch mit einem Vorsprung von fast 23 Prozentpunkten für sich entscheiden konnte.
Coloms 67-jährige Kontrahentin Hyde-Smith rief diesen am späten Mittwochnachmittag an, um ihre Niederlage einzuräumen. Kurze Zeit später veröffentlichte sie eine entsprechende Erklärung.
„Auch wenn dies nicht das Ergebnis ist, auf das wir hingearbeitet oder auf das wir gehofft haben, respektiere ich die Entscheidung der Wähler in Mississippi. Ich möchte Scott Colom gratulieren und ihm alles Gute für die große Verantwortung wünschen“, so Hyde-Smith.
Die neuen Senatorinnen und Senatoren werden in der ersten Januarwoche vereidigt.

https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/.title: India bypasses own rules to buy Israeli phone-hacking tech
https://www.aljazeera.com/features/2026/.text:
India bypasses own rules to buy Israeli phone-hacking tech
India’s expansive surveillance capabilities extend far beyond just cloning phones to accessing cloud-based data from social media platforms like Instagram and Tinder.
New Delhi, India – India has exempted an Israeli phone-hacking company from New Delhi’s own rules, allowing it to sell phone-extraction products and surveillance technology to government agencies and sparking concerns and criticism from rights groups and activists.
An investigation by the digital-rights group Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) found Indian Home Minister Amit Shah, a close confidante of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, signed off on exemptions from “make in India” procurement rules, clearing the way for government forensic institutions to buy at least 422 items of foreign technology, including products made by the Israeli firm Cellebrite.
Modi’s federal government and state governments ruled by his Bharatiya Janata Party are not the only ones who bought this Israeli technology. States governed by the opposition Indian National Congress party, including Himachal Pradesh, Keralam and Karnataka, also purchased similar phone-extraction and cloning tools.
A review of documents revealed that India’s expansive surveillance capabilities extend far beyond just cloning phones and extracting data without passwords to accessing cloud-based data from social media platforms – such as Instagram, X and Tinder – as well as data from connected devices such as Amazon’s Alexa and Google Home.
Experts argued that India’s current laws offer no guardrails against overreaching surveillance and the data extractions happen in a legal grey zone.
“It is clear that there is an expansion of India’s surveillance capabilities and it is becoming both wider and deeper,” said Vrinda Bhandari, a lawyer in the Supreme Court who works on digital rights and privacy issues.
“It’s now easier to conduct mass surveillance rather than targeted, specific surveillance and also possible to do more intrusive surveillance,” she told Al Jazeera. “[Today,] surveillance gives you a richer picture of an individual’s life.”
From Instagram to Tinder: Extracting cloud-based data
The IFF reviewed a letter also seen by Al Jazeera from India’s Ministry of Home Affairs dated January 7 in which Shah signed off on a wide-ranging, one-year waiver of “make in India” rules to clear a path for buying at least 422 forensic items.
Under “make in India” procurement rules, preference must be given to eligible Indian manufacturers over foreign suppliers in awarding government contracts. However, the rules allow exemptions with the approval of the minister in charge of the procuring department.
Another letter by the ministry dated January 20 showed Shah permitted the National Investigation Agency (NIA) to buy Israeli company Cellebrite’s Premium Tool on a three-year licence for about 50 million rupees ($529,947).
In specifications demanded by the government that were revealed in a review of tender bids, “solution” software must be capable of using login tokens recovered from seized phones or computers to access more than 100 cloud services. Login tokens are in effect digital keys that keep users signed in to online accounts.
Although an exemption for a company does not confirm whether a certain product was purchased by any government agency, it points to the range of forensic capabilities that opened up for procurement by Indian agencies.
From the 422-item exemption list, the IFF identified 118 items under digital and multimedia forensics, including Israeli company Cellebrite’s Pathfinder, Inseyets On-Prem Pro and Inseyets Offline.
Cellebrite’s tools have been used against journalists and activists in countries like Serbia, Jordan, Kenya and Russia.
Other products included tools from foreign digital-forensics companies like Magnet, MSAB, Oxygen Forensics and Belkasoft as well as software for open-source intelligence, dark-web monitoring and cryptocurrency investigations.
Al Jazeera reviewed a request for a bid proposal by the Delhi Police for software for its National Cyber Forensic Laboratory, which comes under the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre, an initiative of the Home Ministry.
Consider the capabilities the police department was seeking in its request: software that bypasses passwords on Apple’s macOS, Microsoft Windows and Linux operating systems; recovers internet activity, browser histories, deleted files and identifies traces of VPNs; bypasses screen locks; performs full file system extractions; decrypts backups; and extracts information from messaging applications.
The Delhi Police demanded another “all-in-one” system to access more than 100 cloud services, including Google, Apple, WhatsApp, Instagram, Telegram, Discord and dating platforms such as Tinder, Grindr and OkCupid or platforms like Slack and OnlyFans using account credentials or login tokens recovered from devices. Its specifications also sought the extraction of data from drones, wearable devices and devices like Amazon Alexa and Google Home.
Al Jazeera reached out to officials at the NIA, the Home Ministry and home departments of opposition-ruled states of Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka and Keralam for comments. The Delhi Police reports to Shah’s mInistry.
None of them had responded to Al Jazeera by the time of publication.
‘How did they get inside my phone?’
For some, the lack of transparency in the surveillance capabilities of India’s security agencies is not just a theoretical concern.
Last month, when Modi’s government faced street protests demanding the election chief resign, popular YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, a Modi critic, landed in New Delhi to participate in the demonstrations.
On the morning of the protest, he was detained by Delhi Police while still at home. His phone was taken from him. Speaking on a podcast later, Rathee said he believed police had tried to clone his iPhone using Israeli company Cellebrite’s tools but the attempt may have failed because his device was running a newer version of the iOS operating system than what the tool was capable of tricking.
Al Jazeera could not verify Rathee’s account, but Rathee is not alone in this suspicion.
Mohammad Aslam Hussain, a reporter with the newspaper Siasat Daily, told Al Jazeera that he was detained with a cameraperson on October 10 in New Delhi and his phone was confiscated at the scene.
“When I got my device later in the evening, all recorded footage of our reporting had been selectively deleted from the device,” Hussain said. The reporter uses Samsung’s Android-operated Galaxy S24 secured with a pattern lock and fingerprint authentication.
Hussain added that he cannot say conclusively what tools the police used to bypass his phone’s authentication requirement. “But it raises several questions with no one willing to respond to them,” he added. “How did they get inside my phone?”
The Indian government has faced accusations that it has used sophisticated spyware against journalists, activists, lawyers and political opponents during Modi’s years in power.
In 2019, WhatsApp disclosed that the Pegasus spyware, developed by the Israeli firm NSO Group, had been used to target Indian journalists and human rights defenders. Forensic examinations by Amnesty International later confirmed Pegasus infections on the phones of journalists Siddharth Varadarajan and Anand Mangnale. The government has denied allegations of unauthorised surveillance.
Bhandari told Al Jazeera that another problem in holding overarching surveillance to account is identifying the affected party. Often, she pointed out, the person placed under surveillance “does not know about it, so what does one do?”
‘Friction for surveillance’?
The central legal gap identified by digital rights group IFF is that India has no statute or protocol that specifically authorises or regulates the forced unlocking and full extraction of data from a mobile phone seized by law enforcement agencies.
Existing seizure powers under criminal law do not explicitly address bypassing passcodes, copying an entire file system, harvesting login tokens to access cloud accounts or establishing rules for the retention and deletion of extracted data.
The Supreme Court in a 2017 judgement recognised privacy as a fundamental right under the Indian Constitution. The judgement established that any state intrusion into privacy must have a legal basis, pursue a legitimate state aim and be proportionate to that aim.
Bhandari told Al Jazeera that when the government agencies “deploy these capabilities without any proper meaningful oversight, the net of surveillance is cast wider and deeper and a lot more people are affected without either legislative, parliamentary or judicial oversight”.
Bhandari noted that while some countries like the United Kingdom or Germany “have some element of either parliamentary oversight or judicial oversight, India only has an internal review mechanism in executive oversight”.
“The whole point of having any oversight is to create a friction for surveillance,” she said, “so that it’s not easy for the government to just target everybody.”
“The current legal framework fails in this safeguard,” Bhandari said.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Brasil de Fato conquista Prêmio Folha Verde da Assembleia Legislativa do RS
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O Brasil de Fato RS foi escolhido para receber o 12º Prêmio Folha Verde, da Assembleia Legislativa do Rio Grande do Sul, na categoria Mídia Agrícola. A indicação foi apresentada pelo deputado estadual Adão Pretto Filho (PT), que destacou a atuação do veículo na cobertura das lutas e da produção das famílias do campo. Os vencedores foram definidos pela comissão julgadora na segunda-feira (9).
A cerimônia de entrega está marcada para 14 de dezembro, no Salão Júlio de Castilhos, na Assembleia Legislativa, em Porto Alegre. Antes, o resultado será submetido à homologação da Mesa Diretora e publicado no Diário Oficial.
“O Brasil de Fato é um veículo de comunicação fundamental na pauta da reforma agrária, da agricultura familiar e da transição agroecológica, que é uma das principais pautas do nosso mandato. Esse reconhecimento do parlamento gaúcho é fruto de um trabalho sério feito por profissionais dedicados e comprometidos com a verdade e democracia”, afirmou Pretto Filho.
A editora-chefe do Brasil de Fato RS, Katia Marko, recebeu a notícia com alegria e destacou a importância da reforma agrária popular, da agricultura familiar e da agroecologia para o veículo. “Acreditamos que esse é o caminho para ‘evitarmos o fim do mundo’ e buscamos dar visibilidade a experiências agroecológicas e sustentáveis, mostrando que é possível construir uma nova forma de estar no mundo”, afirmou.
Marko agradeceu a indicação de Pretto Filho e o definiu como parceiro na luta pela democratização da comunicação. “Ele traz essa bandeira de berço, pois seu pai, o deputado federal Adão Pretto, foi um grande defensor da diversidade de vozes e das rádios comunitárias, inclusive cunhou a palavra de ordem: reforma agrária no ar”, destacou.
A editora também celebrou a comunicação popular e manifestou o desejo de novos reconhecimentos ao trabalho dos veículos comprometidos com as lutas sociais: “Viva a comunicação popular e que venham mais e mais reconhecimentos da importância de termos veículos comprometidos com as lutas sociais”.
Valorização das experiências do campo
Instituído em 1995, o Prêmio Folha Verde reconhece pessoas, instituições e empresas pela contribuição ao setor primário e ao desenvolvimento da economia gaúcha. A iniciativa é realizada pela Comissão de Agricultura, Pecuária, Pesca e Cooperativismo da Assembleia, a partir de indicações dos parlamentares.
A escolha dos vencedores ocorreu em reunião aberta ao público, com votação individual e manifestações dos integrantes da comissão julgadora em cada categoria. Presidido pelo deputado estadual Zé Nunes (PT), o colegiado reuniu representantes dos governos estadual e federal, do Sindicato dos Jornalistas Profissionais do Rio Grande do Sul (Sindjors) e dos jornais Correio do Povo e Jornal do Comércio.
Para Nunes, a premiação permite dar visibilidade à diversidade de experiências do campo gaúcho. “É um prêmio muito importante porque permite que cada deputado olhe para a sua região, conheça as experiências e identifique quem está fazendo a diferença. É uma forma de mostrar para todo o Rio Grande do Sul o trabalho de pessoas e organizações que muitas vezes não têm a visibilidade que merecem, mas que são fundamentais para o fortalecimento do nosso setor primário”, destacou.
Reconhecimento em 15 categorias
Além do Brasil de Fato, a edição deste ano contempla organizações de agricultores, trabalhadores rurais, instituições de ensino e pesquisa e iniciativas ligadas à produção de alimentos, à pesca e à preservação ambiental.
Entre os escolhidos está a Cooperativa dos Trabalhadores Assentados da Região de Porto Alegre (Cootap), na categoria Cooperativas Agrícolas. A Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS) receberá duas distinções: pelo Programa de Pós-Graduação em Desenvolvimento Rural, em Setor Agrícola, e pela Estação Experimental Agronômica, em Desenvolvimento Agrário.
Confira a relação completa dos vencedores:
- Setor Agrícola: Programa de Pós-Graduação em Desenvolvimento Rural da UFRGS

- Setor Rural: Associação Gaúcha Pró-Escolas Famílias Agrícolas (Agefa)

https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.author: Mera Aladam
https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/.text:
Morning update
Good morning Middle East Eye readers,
Here are the latest developments:
- Iran’s armed forces have updated their list of possible targets in the case of a renewed war, including having no geographical restrictions on retaliatory strikes. Kioumars Heydari, who serves as the deputy chief of staff of Iran’s armed forces, said that the updated list reflected previous Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s instructions for an "immediate, effective response without geographical limitations" to any threat, warning that Iran's response to any future conflict would be "truly crippling" for the enemy.
- Iran’s top security official Mohsen Rezaei warned that Tehran could strike military bases involved in any renewed US attacks against Iran. "If the US launches another war against Iran, every military base involved in the aggression - from West Asia to Europe - will be a legitimate target for Iran’s lethal strikes," Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said in a post on X.
- US Vice President JD Vance is contemplating having direct talks with Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei, according to US media outlets. Doha could be seen as a possible venue if the meeting goes ahead, the Wall Street Journal reported based on information from several US and Middle Eastern officials as well as sources familiar with the matter.
- Authorities in the UAE's Ras Al Khaimah emirate have announced reopening several beaches following closures prompted by an oil spill from a tanker damaged in a suspected attack in the Gulf last month.
- An Israeli air strike targeting the Nasser Medical Complex in southern Gaza early on Thursday has killed at least six Palestinians and injured more than 50 others. The strike hit the second floor of al-Yasin building within the medical complex, with the hospital’s director indicating that it caused extensive damage to the intensive care and surgical wards.
- Saudi Arabia's civil defence said in a statement that debris from two ballistic missiles intercepted and destroyed after being launched by Yemen's Houthis towards the kingdom's Mecca region fell in the area. The Saudi-led coalition also said it intercepted and destroyed a drone in the kingdom's Riyadh region.

https://www.mediapart.fr/journal/france/.title: Gérard Depardieu accusé d’agression sexuelle: la preuve par l’image
https://www.mediapart.fr/journal/france/.author: Marine Turchi, Laura Wojcik
https://www.mediapart.fr/journal/france/.text:
À quelques jours du procès en appel pour agressions sexuelles de Gérard Depardieu, Mediapart révèle une nouvelle affaire qui fait voler en éclats la défense du célèbre acteur.
Accusé depuis 2018 de violences sexuelles par vingt-deux femmes, mis en examen pour viols et condamné pour des agressions sexuelles sur deux femmes (il a fait appel), le comédien de 77 ans s’est toujours défendu avec un argument : oui, il peut tenir des propos grossiers et potaches, mais non, il n’a jamais touché une femme sans son consentement.
Mais des images et des témoignages inédits montrent l’inverse. Ils concernent le tournage du film Turf (2013), réalisé par Fabien Onteniente. Et notamment une scène tournée le 2 novembre 2011 à l’hippodrome d’Auteuil, aux côtés de 150 figurant·es.
Sur des images que dévoile Le Média et dont Mediapart a pu vérifier l’authenticité, on voit Gérard Depardieu toucher, de manière répétée et insistante, la cuisse, l’entrejambe et les fesses d’une figurante, tandis que celle-ci tente, en vain, de repousser sa main.
Mediapart a retrouvé cette figurante, et elle témoigne pour la première fois, à visage découvert. Elle s’appelle Olivia. À l’époque, elle était étudiante et avait 22 ans. Face à notre caméra, elle raconte comment l’acteur, placé à côté d’elle durant cette scène, n’a cessé de la toucher : « Il met la main sur mes fesses. Sur les deux. Longtemps. [...] Il tente plusieurs fois vraiment ce qu’on peut appeler l’entrejambe », relate-t-elle, affirmant aussi qu’il aurait « mis sa main dans [son] décolleté », lui touchant « la poitrine à plusieurs reprises ».
Elle dit avoir tenté « par tous les moyens de lui enlever » la main, mais il aurait « recommenc[é] derrière ». Elle confie s’être sentie « attaquée », car « [sa] culotte ne suffisait plus pour [la] protéger ». Elle estime avoir subi une « agression ».
Ces gestes de l’acteur ne figurent pas dans le scénario du film, que nous nous sommes procuré.
Gérard Depardieu recadré
Une seule personne est intervenue sur le plateau : la directrice de casting, Fany Touya-Calmon, qui témoigne également pour la première fois face à la caméra de Mediapart. Elle affirme avoir dû « replacer les figurantes » et « calcul[er] [la] longueur de bras » de Gérard Depardieu « pour qu’il ne puisse pas les toucher ». Elle dit avoir dû s’« accroupir » aux pieds du comédien pour « rester là pendant toutes les prises qui [ont suivi] ». Son témoignage est confirmé à Mediapart par deux membres de son équipe, ainsi que par Olivia.
La directrice de casting dit avoir prévenu à la fois le directeur de production et le réalisateur, Fabien Onteniente. Elle affirme que la production aurait décidé de ne rien faire, minimisant les faits, et que le réalisateur a en revanche « agi » en allant voir Gérard Depardieu « à la fin de la journée ».
Ce que Fabien Onteniente avait confirmé à Mediapart lors de notre première enquête, en 2023. Il nous avait assuré que la figurante était venue le voir « en larmes » et qu’il était allé « engueuler » Gérard Depardieu en ces termes : « Je lui ai dit : “Tu ne recommences pas ça. C’est fini, je ne veux pas être emmerdé avec toutes tes conneries, tu te comportes bien ! […] Tu te rends compte de ce que tu fais, là ? La caméra était en contre-plongée, on peut voir ce que tu fais, tu te rends compte de l’image que tu renvoies ?” » Selon lui, l’acteur se serait montré « penaud » et aurait « fait l’enfant qui a fait une bêtise ».
Contactés, les producteurs de Turf – Chez Wam, la société d’Alain Chabat, et Pathé – et le directeur de production, Bruno Vatin, n’ont pas répondu. En 2023, celui-ci nous avait indiqué n’avoir « aucun souvenir de cet événement ». « Ce fut un tournage chaotique pour moi, vu le nombre de problèmes que j’ai eu à gérer, il est possible que ma mémoire fasse défaut », nous avait-il déclaré.
D’après plusieurs témoignages que Mediapart a recueillis, lors du montage du film, il a été difficile de trouver des images utilisables de cette séquence. « Sur trois ou quatre prises, la figurante faisait une tête pas possible, elle avait vraiment l’air mal, sa jupe bougeait », a rapporté une membre de l’équipe de postproduction. « J’ai eu du mal à trouver une prise où la figurante ne s’est pas écartée de Depardieu », a expliqué une autre.
Sollicité à plusieurs reprises par le biais de ses avocat·es, Delphine Meillet et David-Olivier Kaminski, Gérard Depardieu ne nous a pas répondu. Déjà questionné par Mediapart en 2023 sur des accusations de violences sexuelles lors de onze tournages – notamment Turf –, l’acteur avait fait savoir, par la voix de son avocat de l’époque, qu’il « dément[ait] l’ensemble des accusations susceptibles de relever de la loi pénale ».
Un agenda judiciaire chargé
Nos révélations interviennent à un moment clé pour Gérard Depardieu. Le 16 novembre, s’ouvre le procès en appel de l’acteur dans l’affaire du film Les Volets verts, qu’avait révélée Mediapart. En 2025, le comédien avait été condamné pour avoir agressé sexuellement deux femmes sur le tournage de ce film, en 2021. Il conteste les faits et a fait appel.
Dans un autre dossier – les accusations de viols de la comédienne Charlotte Arnould, pour lesquelles il est mis en examen –, on saura, le 26 novembre, si Gérard Depardieu sera jugé devant la cour criminelle de Paris. En septembre 2025, la juge d’instruction chargée de l’affaire avait ordonné un procès pour viols. Mais l’acteur a fait appel de cette décision, et la chambre de l’instruction de la cour d’appel de Paris doit désormais se prononcer.
Gérard Depardieu, qui bénéficie de la présomption d’innocence, a toujours contesté l’ensemble des accusations le visant. Dans une tribune publiée dans Le Figaro en 2023, le comédien avait affirmé qu’il n’avait « jamais au grand jamais abusé d’une femme », et que « faire du mal à une femme, ce serait comme donner des coups de pied dans le ventre de [s]a propre mère ».
En mars 2025, lors de son procès, il avait nié fermement toute agression sexuelle. « Je ne vais pas m’amuser à 76 ans, à 150 kilos, à mettre la main aux fesses. Je ne suis pas Émile Louis, avait-il déclaré, en référence au tueur et violeur en série de l’Yonne. Je ne vois pas pourquoi je m’amuserais à peloter une femme, des fesses, des seins, je ne suis pas un frotteur dans le métro. »

https://www.humanite.fr/monde/immigratio.title: Suspension des aides, durcissement des règles : les sauvetages en Méditerranée rendus quasi impossibles
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/immigratio.author: Lina Sankari
https://www.humanite.fr/monde/immigratio.text:
Sortie des radars médiatiques, la question des morts en Méditerranée demeure vive. La restriction croissante de l’action humanitaire par des pays européens multiplie le nombre de disparitions et de décès de migrants qui fuient la guerre.
Dans l’histoire qu’elle se raconte à elle-même, l’Union européenne (UE) se vit comme une citadelle assiégée de toutes parts. Moins nombreux à fouler le sol européen depuis quelques années, les migrants sont toutefois plus nombreux à mourir en Méditerranée. « Au cours des quatre premiers mois de 2026, le nombre de morts ou de disparus en mer Méditerranée centrale a plus que doublé par rapport à la même période en 2025, atteignant 821 personnes. Dans le même temps, les arrivées par cet itinéraire, principalement en Italie, ont chuté de 46 %, passant à 8 577 », note l’ONU.
Le sauvetage dans cette zone, réputée comme l’une des plus dangereuses au monde, pâtit de la suspension des subventions publiques accordées aux ONG de secours...

https://taz.de/Die-Wahrheit/!6229139/.title: Die Wahrheit: Tumult um Ungeduld
https://taz.de/Die-Wahrheit/!6229139/.author: Holger Paetz
https://taz.de/Die-Wahrheit/!6229139/.text:
Die Wahrheit: Tumult um Ungeduld
Donnerstag ist Gedichtetag auf der Wahrheit: Heute darf sich die geneigte Leserschaft an einem Gedicht über eine politische Binse erfreuen.
Mann, wenn man dich nach Fehlern fragt,
bekenne dich gleich schuldig.
Sprich leise, aber nicht verzagt:
Ich bin so ungeduldig.
So einer gilt als Pläneschmied.
Agil, vital, energisch.
Selbst wenn man auf Entfernung sieht:
Der Typ ist end-lethargisch.
Auch wenn du’s kaum mehr schaffst vom Stuhl,
und immer nur mit Ächzen,
viel lieber zwischen Zehen puhlst,
du solltest weiter krächzen:
Die Ungeduld, die Ungeduld,
die hat mich angetrieben.
Hat mich befeuert und geschult.
Sonst ist mir nichts geblieben.
Die Ungeduld? Spricht drauf der Tod.
Die darf’s gern weiter treiben.
Ich werd dich, so als Angebot,
am besten gleich entleiben.
O nein, Herr Tod, das bitte muss
so schnell jetzt nicht! Seid gnädig!
Nee, sagt der Tod. Wir machen Schluss.
Dann ist das auch erledigt.
Die Wahrheit auf taz.de
Die Wahrheit
ist die einzige Satire- und Humorseite einer Tageszeitung weltweit.
Die Wahrheit
hat den einzigartigen Cartoonstreifen: ©Tom Touché.
Die Wahrheit
hat drei Grundsätze:
Warum sachlich, wenn es persönlich geht.
Warum recherchieren, wenn man schreiben kann.
Warum beweisen, wenn man behaupten kann.
Deshalb weiß Die Wahrheit immer, wie weit man zu weit gehen kann.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.title: Ten police officers, 18 fighters killed in northwest Pakistan attack
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/1.text:
Ten police officers, 18 fighters killed in northwest Pakistan attack
Officers were returning from a mine in the Gumbat area of Kohat district when fighters opened fire on them, authorities say.
Gunmen have attacked police officers conducting an operation against illegal gold mining in northwestern Pakistan, with 10 officers and 18 fighters killed in the ensuing violence.
A statement by provincial police in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa said officers were returning from a mine in the Gumbat area of Kohat district on Wednesday when armed men opened fire on them.
In addition to the dozens killed, 12 police personnel were wounded, the statement said.
Hours later, the Pakistani Taliban issued a statement claiming the attack.
Earlier, a senior administrative official in Kohat told the AFP news agency that fighters had set two police vehicles on fire during the assault, while two other police vehicles and one private vehicle were missing.
Another senior administrative official in the Orakzai area of Kohat said that 10 fighters belonging to the Pakistan Taliban were killed during a separate operation in the district.
A large quantity of weapons was also recovered from the fighters, the official said.
A spokesman for a local emergency service said earlier on Wednesday that there had been a “firing incident involving police personnel” in Kohat district, adding that rescue workers were treating a dozen wounded officers.
Security forces are battling intensifying violence in the border province that they say emanates from Afghanistan, an accusation the Taliban government in Kabul rejects.
Ongoing attacks
The Pakistan Taliban, formerly known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, have stepped up attacks on security forces in the region in recent months.
Pakistan has seen a surge in violence in recent years, much of it blamed on the TTP.
The group is separate from but closely allied with the Afghan Taliban, who returned to power in neighbouring Afghanistan in 2021.
Relations between Pakistan and Afghanistan have been fraught since the Afghan Taliban retook power, and worsened after deadly border clashes in October last year that led to near-total closure of the border.
Pakistan frequently accuses Afghanistan’s Taliban government of sheltering TTP fighters, an allegation Kabul denies.
Hundreds of civilians have been killed in fighting between the two countries in the last year, according to figures from the United Nations mission in Afghanistan.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: MST realiza 3ª Feira Estadual da Reforma Agrária em Goiás neste final de semana
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: João Palhares
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O Movimento dos Trabalhadores Rurais Sem Terra (MST) realiza neste sábado e domingo, 14 e 15 de novembro, a 3ª Feira Estadual da Reforma Agrária de Goiás, em Goiânia. A programação, que será realizada na Praça Universitária, na região central da capital, tem início às 10h. Durante os dois dias, quem passar pela Feira encontrará alimentos produzidos em assentamentos e acampamentos do estado, pratos da culinária da terra e um palco com artistas sem terra.
Cerca de 30 bancas devem receber a produção das regiões onde o MST tem assentamentos e acampamentos em Goiás. Laticínios, geleias, mel, artesanato e outros itens fabricados nas áreas do movimento, ocupam a lista de produtos produzidos pelas comunidades e que estarão disponíveis. “Tudo que é produzido dentro das nossas áreas vai ser exposto lá”, explica Leandro Costa, coordenador nacional do MST em Goiás.
O propósito da feira é mostrar que a luta pela terra não termina na conquista do lote. “Quando a gente faz uma feira, a gente coloca um pouco dessa história nossa de luta pela terra, que é a gente querer de fato um pedaço de chão para plantar e produzir alimentos saudáveis, sem veneno, sem agrotóxico”, complementa. A produção sem agrotóxicos é hoje a política do movimento para o modo de produzir em suas áreas, e é esse o critério dos produtos que vão estar à venda.
Mostrar à cidade sobre qual possibilidade de mundo o Movimento quer não deixa de ser um dos pontos também da ocupação. Ainda conforme Leandro, a construção popular da Feira busca mostrar que “a reforma agrária que a gente quer não é a reforma agrária clássica. É a reforma agrária social, popular, onde a gente vem desenvolvendo uma relação com o meio ambiente, uma relação com a produção saudável, eliminando a questão da especulação da terra”, explica.
A Feira chega à terceira edição depois de dois encontros anuais desde 2024. A edição do ano passado, em dezembro, foi um momento de comemoração dupla: as famílias do acampamento Dom Tomás Balduíno, em Formosa, anunciaram a posse definitiva da Fazenda Crixás, depois de mais de uma década de ocupações, reocupações, disputas judiciais e um período acampadas à beira da BR-060.
“É uma feira que a gente agora pretende fazer todo ano”, explicou Leandro. A edição deste ano acontece após ele e o vereador de Goiânia Fabrício Rosa (PT) serem presos pela Polícia Militar do Estado de Goiás (PMGO) durante um ato pelos 30 anos do Massacre de Eldorado dos Carajás na GO-210, em Santa Helena de Goiás. À época, os dois foram soltos no mesmo dia, e os processos abertos contra eles, por constrangimento ilegal no caso de Leandro e por desacato e desobediência no de Fabrício, foram arquivados pela Justiça entre junho e julho. Já a atuação dos policiais passou a ser investigada pela Corregedoria da PM e pelo MP de Goiás.
Samba, viola e capoeira
A programação cultural começa no sábado (14) às 11h30, com Dona Neuma do Samba e sua batucada. Às 13h, uma roda de viola homenageia Seu Bodim, artista sem terra que morava no Acampamento Dona Neura, em Hidrolândia, que encantou-se recentemente. A tarde segue com apresentações de artistas sem terra, dança afro às 15h e gincana infantil entre 16h15 e 17h15. À noite, a roda de samba vai das 17h30 às 19h30, e o Forrozim Delis encerra o sábado, das 20h às 22h.
No domingo (15), a feira abre às 9h com uma roda de Capoeira Angola. A batucada do Bloco do Caçador se apresenta às 11h, e artistas sem terra ocupam o palco ao longo do dia. “É muito importante para nós expor os nossos produtos numa feira cheia de mística, cheia de culturas diferentes, com muita festa e com muita alegria. É trazer a nossa cultura sem terra e mostrar por que a gente faz a luta pela terra”, conta Leandro.
É dessa cultura sem terra que a juventude do MST cuida em boa parte da Feira. Organizados num coletivo próprio, os jovens estão à frente da cultura e da comunicação do evento e também ajudam a organizá-lo como um todo, conta Taynara Viana, da coordenação nacional do MST em Goiás. “Tanto a cultura quanto a comunicação, para nós do MST, vêm como esse movimento de resistência contra a mídia hegemônica, que a gente sabe que muitas vezes distorce, omite informações e não é nem um pouco neutra. Então, a gente traz a voz dos movimentos sociais, da luta popular”, afirma.
Cultura essa que atravessa os símbolos de resistência do movimento e também aparece nos artistas da música, do teatro, da dança, da poesia e dos contos. “Como o MST está hoje em quase todo o território nacional, cada estado também cria e coloca um pouco da sua cultura nessa cultura sem terra. E vai compondo essa diversidade imensa que a gente tem no movimento”, finaliza Taynara.

https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/pales.title: Palestinian families brace for expulsion as settlers erect outpost near West Bank village
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/pales.author: Tamara Davison
https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/pales.text:
Palestinian families brace for expulsion as settlers erect outpost near West Bank village
Mohammed* sips coffee outside his small concrete home in the al-Shuneh cluster, framed by the sprawling Jordan Valley in the occupied West Bank.
But the energy abruptly shifts when a pickup truck kicks up dust and hurtles down the hillside: it’s Israeli settlers.
He quickly ushers his guests toward the door, watching anxiously until the car passes into the distance.
“The attacks are escalating,” the Palestinian man says, his young children cautiously peering out of the doorway of his family home.
“There's this feeling of insecurity, living in this constant limbo.”

Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
Around 80 Palestinian families rely on the remote rocky hillside on the eastern slopes of the West Bank, overlooking the Jordan River.
Al-Shuneh is one of the four population clusters in the agricultural village of Jiftlik, north of the city of Jericho.
The village's population consists of farmers and nomads who rely on livestock raising for their livelihoods.
'He told me... I should go to Europe, Canada, or places like that'
- Mohammed, al-Shuneh resident
Many were born in al-Shuneh to families displaced by Israeli forces decades ago from other parts of Palestine.
But their livelihoods have been upended by a slow and ongoing torment: lingering Israeli demolition orders and, more recently, the subsequent arrival of hostile settlers.
As Israel headed to the polls on 27 October for parliamentary elections, al-Shuneh was disrupted by the sight of new tents and Israeli flags mounted on the hilltop just two minutes away from Mohammed’s home, adding to an already growing atmosphere of intimidation.
The armed group installed water and electricity cables and released a video featuring drone footage, settler interviews, and clips of a mother with a young baby on social media, encouraging others to join them.
It’s one of the latest Israeli outposts established in the Jordan Valley, which are illegal under both Israeli domestic law and international law.
According to the townspeople, the message delivered in the run-up to the outpost’s establishment was clear: “If [Benjamin] Netanyahu wins, leave on your own. If [Gadi] Eisenkot wins, we will make sure you are displaced.”
While votes were still being counted in Israel on 28 October, masked settlers encircled several homes in the early hours of the morning, threatening the families.
“You don't know what the future holds, or where you'll be tomorrow,” Mohammed tells Middle East Eye. “Your hands are shackled.”
The Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission said Israeli settlers attempted to establish 28 new outposts and committed 1,369 attacks in October alone across the West Bank.
It’s a sign that Israeli settler strategies are escalating rapidly despite political shifts.
At this outpost, settler numbers are thought to have risen to almost 20 in the days after its establishment, and aggressive rhetoric is growing.
When Mohammed asked one of the settlers walking on his land where else he was supposed to go, he was told anywhere but his homeland.
“He told me that there’s no future for my children here or me, and that I should go to Europe, Canada, or places like that.”
Fears of forced displacement
The road towards al-Shuneh on the outskirts of Jiftlik meanders through rolling hills, past date forests and settlements emblazoned with Israeli flags. Along the way, the empty shells of destroyed buildings that once housed other thriving Palestinian villages increasingly come into view. 
A short while from Mohammed’s home, another family sits outside a small building, watching the settlers walk along the nearby hilltop. 
Children pass on their way home from school: a 2km walk on which students have also encountered threatening settlers.
Nearby, Osama Dueis sits beside a large stack of chairs in preparation for an upcoming wedding; but even as they prepare to celebrate, Dueis fears his family will be displaced a second time.
His first home was destroyed by the settlers in a nearby village now largely flattened and desolate, forcing him toward Jiftlik with his family and livestock just last month.
They’ve barely had time to even make the building, a tight fit for six extended families, feel like home, but Dueis senses the weight of another looming potential displacement.
“I mean, look at our situation, we’re left living under a plastic sheet; it’s barely a life, but we have no other choice,” he tells MEE.
“We can’t speak out, we can’t go anywhere, we can’t even head into the mountains, nothing. Everything is so expensive - livestock feed, everything.
“There’s no such thing as privacy; nothing is private, it’s just a daily reality,” he adds about the constant monitoring and drones.
'We can’t speak out, we can’t go anywhere, we can’t even head into the mountains, nothing'
- Osama Dueis, al-Shuneh resident
That morning, villagers captured images of the young settlers using binoculars to monitor the town, and in more recent days, the settlers attempted to steal local sheep and have thrown rocks at the Palestinians.
They’ve now decided to keep watch together, working in rotation among the families to monitor any provocations throughout the night.
Beyond the tense exchanges, there have also been violent altercations and the poisoning of livestock.
The targeting of Palestinian farmers, they argue, is not only affecting people’s livelihoods but also having repercussions across the West Bank, as reports suggest settler attacks have contributed to rising livestock costs.
“The settlers in this area… are exceptionally aggressive, even more so than others,” Dueis said, though no arrests have been made.
“They even targeted one of my cousins. After beating him, they asked, 'Do you know how many lives are on [my] conscience?' They take pride in this; they revel in it.”
Demolition orders and restrictions
It’s not just the new settlers placing pressure on the Palestinian residents of the Jordan Valley, whose homes are in Area C under the Oslo Accords, under Israeli security and administrative control.
Even basic improvements to homes or infrastructure have left the community vulnerable to accusations of unauthorised construction, which is heavily restricted by Israel for Palestinians in Area C.
Recent rains blocked local roads, but residents fear even using their tractors to clear the debris would be penalised.
And the challenges aren’t contained to Palestinian communities.
Medical Aid for Palestinians (MAP), a British NGO supporting Jiftlik, said that the mobile clinics they run among rural communities with limited access to healthcare have faced considerable delays due to checkpoints and route closures. On some days, the mobile medical clinics can’t deploy at all due to security risks.
"What we're seeing in communities like al-Shuneh is apartheid in its most blatant form,” Aseel Baidoun, deputy director of communications at MAP, told MEE.
“Settlers can get water and electricity connected within days, while Palestinians wait years for the same basic services and live under constant threat of being driven from their land. This has a direct impact on people's health, but it also makes it harder for us to get care for those who need it.”
The harassment in Jiftlik is part of a broader surge in settler attacks that have displaced thousands of Palestinians across the West Bank since October 2023.
The escalating violence has been met with growing international scrutiny.
Last month, the UK expanded its sanction powers over those enabling illegal Israeli outposts in the West Bank.
Then just one day before the Israeli elections, a United Nations inquiry ruled that Israel had carried out war crimes and crimes against humanity in occupied Palestinian territories, including the systematic targeting of Palestinians across the West Bank.
Yet international condemnation and political developments have done little to change conditions on the ground.
Eisenkot, a former army chief tasked with forming a government, supports West Bank settlements, although he has criticised unauthorised outposts and what he calls “Jewish terror” against Palestinian communities. Whether the new outpost near Jiftlik can be contained remains unclear.
For Palestinians in al-Shuneh, daily life continues in the shadow of an outpost that looms over their homes and continues to expand. As Israel’s political elite jostle to form a government, little offers residents hope of relief. The settlers’ warning still hangs over the community: no political change will save them.
“Based on what we have observed in other communities, we anticipate that, moving forward, the aggression, restrictions, and acts of violence will only increase,” Dueis says.
“There are no options; whether you head north or south, it’s all the same; everywhere you turn, there’s nowhere to go.”
*Name has been changed to protect the identity
